literature.headline_zh: 禽流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期禽流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 免疫抑制仓鼠的感染导致严重疾病,其特征是病毒复制延长、神经侵袭和 75% 死亡率,但未检测到直接接触 死亡率。安慰剂治疗的仓鼠表现出 50% 死亡率。Baloxavir 可实现 100% 存活,缩短病毒脱落时间,减少病毒复制和肺部炎症反应,并预防神经侵袭。高剂量molnupiravir还可以预防死亡率并实现肺和脑组织中的病毒清除。与奥司他韦和低剂量莫努匹拉韦单一疗法相比,联合治疗的存活率达到 75%,并且同样实现了两种组织中的病毒清除,发病率降低。 [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014796]
大多数情况下观察到初始种群数量下降,中位下降17%(四分位数范围-35%至5%),但40个案例中只有8个发现平均种群数量显着减少,只有两个案例种群趋势显着下降。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0360235]
结果表明,暴发 发生在 野生鸟类、高 暴发 通知率、国家、星期几和国定假日都与延迟的 暴发 报告时间相关。根据世界银行的定义,较高的政治稳定性和更好的腐败控制也与较长的报告时间相关,而较高的人均国民总收入和当地家禽密度则与较短的报告延迟相关。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0360917]
研究报告称,禽流感疫情导致供应收缩,市场价格通胀压力加大,人口购买力下降。 [10.66073/refocus-conf/1311049]
聚合酶检测鉴定出人类 IAV 亚基,特别是 H1N1 PA 或 H3N2 PB2,可增加 H5N1 聚合酶活性。 [10.1073/pnas.2631654123]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.headline_en: Recent Avian influenza A viruses literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Infection in immunosuppressed hamsters caused severe disease characterized by prolonged viral replication, neuroinvasion, and 75% mortality, with no direct-contact transmission detected. Placebo-treated hamsters exhibited 50% mortality. [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014796]

Initial population count declines were observed in most cases, with a median decrease of 17% (Inter-quartile range −35% to 5%), but significant reductions in average population counts were detected in only eight of the 40 cases, and a significant decrease in population trend in only two cases. [10.1371/journal.pone.0360235]

The results indicated that outbreaks occurring in wild birds, high outbreak notification rates, country, day of week and national holidays were all associated with delayed outbreak reporting times. [10.1371/journal.pone.0360917]

Oseltamivir treatment was associated with a lower hazard of death than no documented anti-influenza antiviral treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 0.51, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.77). [10.51542/ijscia.v7i5.22]

The study reports that avian influenza epidemics led to a contraction of supply, increased inflationary pressure on market prices, and a decline in the population’s purchasing power. [10.66073/refocus-conf/1311049]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期禽流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。

免疫抑制仓鼠的感染导致严重疾病,其特征是病毒复制延长、神经侵袭和 75% 死亡率,但未检测到直接接触 死亡率。安慰剂治疗的仓鼠表现出 50% 死亡率。Baloxavir 可实现 100% 存活,缩短病毒脱落时间,减少病毒复制和肺部炎症反应,并预防神经侵袭。高剂量molnupiravir还可以预防死亡率并实现肺和脑组织中的病毒清除。与奥司他韦和低剂量莫努匹拉韦单一疗法相比,联合治疗的存活率达到 75%,并且同样实现了两种组织中的病毒清除,发病率降低。
大多数情况下观察到初始种群数量下降,中位下降17%(四分位数范围-35%至5%),但40个案例中只有8个发现平均种群数量显着减少,只有两个案例种群趋势显着下降。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0360235]。
结果表明,暴发 发生在 野生鸟类、高 暴发 通知率、国家、星期几和国定假日都与延迟的 暴发 报告时间相关。根据世界银行的定义,较高的政治稳定性和更好的腐败控制也与较长的报告时间相关,而较高的人均国民总收入和当地家禽密度则与较短的报告延迟相关。
研究报告称,禽流感疫情导致供应收缩,市场价格通胀压力加大,人口购买力下降。 [10.66073/refocus-conf/1311049]。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
Infection in immunosuppressed hamsters caused severe disease characterized by prolonged viral replication, neuroinvasion, and 75% mortality, with no direct-contact transmission detected.

Initial population count declines were observed in most cases, with a median decrease of 17% (Inter-quartile range −35% to 5%), but significant reductions in average population counts were detected in only eight of the 40 cases, and a significant decrease in population trend in only two cases.

Oseltamivir treatment was associated with a lower hazard of death than no documented anti-influenza antiviral treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 0.51, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.77). [10.51542/ijscia.v7i5.22].
literature.zh: 本期禽流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。；免疫抑制仓鼠的感染导致严重疾病,其特征是病毒复制延长、神经侵袭和 75% 死亡率,但未检测到直接接触 死亡率。安慰剂治疗的仓鼠表现出 50% 死亡率。Baloxavir 可实现 100% 存活,缩短病毒脱落时间,减少病毒复制和肺部炎症反应,并预防神经侵袭。高剂量molnupiravir还可以预防死亡率并实现肺和脑组织中的病毒清除。与奥司他韦和低剂量莫努匹拉韦单一疗法相比,联合治疗的存活率达到 75%,并且同样实现了两种组织中的病毒清除,发病率降低。；大多数情况下观察到初始种群数量下降,中位下降17%(四分位数范围-35%至5%),但40个案例中只有8个发现平均种群数量显着减少,只有两个案例种群趋势显着下降。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0360235]。；结果表明,暴发 发生在 野生鸟类、高 暴发 通知率、国家、星期几和国定假日都与延迟的 暴发 报告时间相关。根据世界银行的定义,较高的政治稳定性和更好的腐败控制也与较长的报告时间相关,而较高的人均国民总收入和当地家禽密度则与较短的报告延迟相关。；研究报告称,禽流感疫情导致供应收缩,市场价格通胀压力加大,人口购买力下降。 [10.66073/refocus-conf/1311049]。
literature.en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments. Infection in immunosuppressed hamsters caused severe disease characterized by prolonged viral replication, neuroinvasion, and 75% mortality, with no direct-contact transmission detected. Initial population count declines were observed in most cases, with a median decrease of 17% (Inter-quartile range −35% to 5%), but significant reductions in average population counts were detected in only eight of the 40 cases, and a significant decrease in population trend in only two cases. The results indicated that outbreaks occurring in wild birds, high outbreak notification rates, country, day of week and national holidays were all associated with delayed outbreak reporting times. Oseltamivir treatment was associated with a lower hazard of death than no documented anti-influenza antiviral treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 0.51, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.77). [10.51542/ijscia.v7i5.22].

news.headline_en: Recent Avian influenza A viruses news
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Avian influenza A viruses news developments.
key_findings_en: A study identified twelve distinct genotypes of avian influenza viruses circulating in Laos between 2019 and 2024. The findings were reported by Bioengineer.org on November 12, 2026, and are based on genomic sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. [news-a2594c240ed81dca]
Oregon logs its first H5N1 case in cows; farmer’s union says human avian flu cases underreported in Washington. [news-29f3ff85f36f4f4e]

The United Farm Workers (UFW) warned that the true number of US dairy workers infected with H5N1 bird flu is significantly higher than official government figures show. The union highlighted that many workers are falling ill without being tested due to fear and financial pressure. [news-e33d9250d6c33f31]

A resurgence of human cases of avian influenza A (H5N1) in Cambodia was reported, with the first case involving an 11-year-old who died from severe pneumonia. Scientists suggest that the virus may have gained new genetic material through reassortment, potentially increasing its ability to infect humans. [news-0b1c3fd1861db6c7]

A comprehensive study mapped the adaptive landscape of avian influenza A(H9N2) hemagglutinin, revealing specific amino acid substitution hotspots that govern viral cross-species potential, antibody evasion, and environmental thermostability. The research was reported by Bioengineer.org. [news-aa6c32902e50e8bf]

papers.title: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses continue to expand their geographic and host range, raising concerns about zoonotic transmission and pandemic preparedness. Immunocompromised individuals often develop severe and prolonged disease, yet evidence guiding antiviral therapy remains limited. Here, we characterized the pathogenesis and assessed direct-contact transmission of an influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 virus recently isolated from a human case in British Columbia, Canada, in cyclophosphamide-immunosuppressed hamsters, with normal hamsters included for comparison of infection outcomes and viral shedding kinetics. We also evaluated the antiviral efficacy of oseltamivir (20 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days), baloxavir (50 mg/kg, 2 doses), and molnupiravir (50 or 200 mg/kg twice daily) as monotherapies or in combination (oseltamivir with low-dose molnupiravir) in immunosuppressed hamsters. While normal hamsters showed no mortality and achieved viral clearance, infection in immunosuppressed hamsters caused severe disease characterized by prolonged viral replication, neuroinvasion, and 75% mortality, with no direct-contact transmission detected. In the antiviral efficacy experiment, placebo-treated hamsters exhibited 50% mortality. Baloxavir resulted in 100% survival, shortened viral shedding, reduced viral replication and pulmonary inflammatory responses, and prevented neuroinvasion. High-dose molnupiravir also prevented mortality and achieved viral clearance in lung and brain tissues. Combination therapy resulted in 75% survival and similarly achieved viral clearance in both tissues, with reduced morbidity compared with oseltamivir and low-dose molnupiravir monotherapies. Oseltamivir resulted in 75% survival but failed to prevent severe clinical signs or reduce tissue viral titers, whereas low-dose molnupiravir showed outcomes comparable to placebo. These findings demonstrate the high pathogenicity of a human A(H5N1) isolate in immunosuppressed hamsters, support baloxavir as an effective therapeutic option, and identify molnupiravir-based regimens as promising strategies for severe influenza A(H5N1) infection.

Immunocompromised individuals often develop severe and prolonged disease, yet evidence guiding antiviral therapy remains limited. Here, we characterized the pathogenesis and assessed direct-contact transmission of an influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 virus recently isolated from a human case in British Columbia, Canada, in cyclophosphamide-immunosuppressed hamsters, with normal hamsters included for comparison of infection outcomes and viral shedding kinetics. We also evaluated the antiviral efficacy of oseltamivir (20 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days), baloxavir (50 mg/kg, 2 doses), and molnupiravir (50 or 200 mg/kg twice daily) as monotherapies or in combination (oseltamivir with low-dose molnupiravir) in immunosuppressed hamsters. While normal hamsters showed no mortality and achieved viral clearance, infection in immunosuppressed hamsters caused severe disease characterized by prolonged viral replication, neuroinvasion, and 75% mortality, with no direct-contact transmission detected. In the antiviral efficacy experiment, placebo-treated hamsters exhibited 50% mortality. Baloxavir resulted in 100% survival, shortened viral shedding, reduced viral replication and pulmonary inflammatory responses, and prevented neuroinvasion. High-dose molnupiravir also prevented mortality and achieved viral clearance in lung and brain tissues. Combination therapy resulted in 75% survival and similarly achieved viral clearance in both tissues, with reduced morbidity compared with oseltamivir and low-dose molnupiravir monotherapies. Oseltamivir resulted in 75% survival but failed to prevent severe clinical signs or reduce tissue viral titers, whereas low-dose molnupiravir showed outcomes comparable to placebo. These findings demonstrate the high pathogenicity of a human A(H5N1) isolate in immunosuppressed hamsters, support baloxavir as an effective therapeutic option, and identify molnupiravir-based regimens as promising strategies for severe influenza A(H5N1) infection.

papers.title: Immunogenicity and safety of two priming doses of an MF59-adjuvanted cell-based H5N8 influenza vaccine in healthy persons aged ≥18 years
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Increased transmission of avian influenza from animals to humans has elevated the risk of an H5 pandemic. METHODS: This phase 2, randomized, observer-blind, multi-center trial assessed the immunogenicity and safety of homologous priming with an MF59-adjuvanted, cell-based H5N8 A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 clade 2.3.4.4b vaccine (aH5N8c). We enrolled adults age ≥18 years, equally stratified into 18-64 (including a poultry-worker subset) and ≥65 year cohorts. Primary and secondary outcomes were homologous antibody responses against H5N8 measured in all participants by hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and in a subset by microneutralization (MN) assays on Days 1, 22, and 43. Solicited adverse events (AEs) were monitored for 7 days post-vaccination, with unsolicited AEs tracked throughout Day 43. RESULTS: 239 participants were vaccinated (18-64 years, n = 121; ≥65 years, n = 118). At Day 43 (21 days post second aH5N8c dose), geometric mean fold increases (GMFI) were 13.7 for the 18-64 cohort and 10.2 for the ≥65 cohort. HI seroconversion rates were 75.8% (95% CI 66.1-83.8%) for the 18-64 cohort and 71.0% (61.1-79.6%) for the ≥65 cohort. HI titers ≥1:40 were achieved in 75.8% (66.1-83.8%) and 73.0% (63.2-81.4%) of participants, respectively. MN seroconversion rates were 80.6% (68.6-89.6%) and 70.0% (56.8-81.2%), while MN titers ≥1:40 were 83.9% (72.3-92.0%) and 86.7% (75.4-94.1%), respectively. No notable differences in immune responses by poultry worker status were observed. Most solicited AEs were mild or moderate, resolving within 3 days. Unsolicited AEs were reported by 16.7% participants by Day 43. CONCLUSION: These data support the use of the MF59-adjuvanted, cell-based monovalent H5N8 vaccine as a public health intervention against H5 influenza.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Increased transmission of avian influenza from animals to humans has elevated the risk of an H5 pandemic. This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of an MF59-adjuvanted cell-based H5N8 vaccine in healthy adults.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This phase 2, randomized, observer-blind, multi-center trial assessed the immunogenicity and safety of the vaccine in adults aged ≥18 years, equally stratified into 18-64 and ≥65 year cohorts, including a poultry-worker subset.

No notable differences in immune responses by poultry worker status were observed. Most solicited AEs were mild or moderate, resolving within 3 days.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that two priming doses of the MF59-adjuvanted cell-based H5N8 vaccine induce robust immune responses in both age groups, with no significant differences in efficacy by poultry worker status.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide important data for the development and implementation of vaccines against H5N8 influenza, supporting their use as a public health intervention in at-risk populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on healthy adults and the absence of long-term follow-up. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on a single trial with no additional comparative data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of an MF59-adjuvanted cell-based H5N8 vaccine in healthy adults aged ≥18 years. It was a phase 2, randomized, observer-blind, multi-center trial that enrolled participants into two age cohorts, including a poultry-worker subset. The primary outcomes were antibody responses measured by hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and microneutralization (MN) assays, with solicited adverse events monitored for 7 days and unsolicited events tracked up to Day 43. The results showed robust immune responses, with HI seroconversion rates of 75.8% and 71.0% in the 18-64 and ≥65 year cohorts, respectively. MN seroconversion rates were 80.6% and 70.0%, with titers ≥1:40 achieved in 83.9% and 86.7% of participants. No significant differences in immune responses were observed by poultry worker status. Most adverse events were mild or moderate, and unsolicited events were reported by 16.7% of participants. The study supports the use of the vaccine as a public health intervention against H5N8 influenza, though its findings are limited to healthy adults and lack long-term follow-up.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Increased transmission of avian influenza from animals to humans has elevated the risk of an H5 pandemic. This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of an MF59-adjuvanted cell-based H5N8 vaccine in healthy adults.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: This phase 2, randomized, observer-blind, multi-center trial assessed the immunogenicity and safety of the vaccine in adults aged ≥18 years, equally stratified into 18-64 and ≥65 year cohorts, including a poultry-worker subset.
elements_en.methods: Primary and secondary outcomes were homologous antibody responses against H5N8 measured in all participants by hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and in a subset by microneutralization (MN) assays on Days 1, 22, and 43. Solicited adverse events (AEs) were monitored for 7 days post-vaccination, with unsolicited AEs tracked throughout Day 43.
elements_en.main_results: 239 participants were vaccinated (18-64 years, n = 121; ≥65 years, n = 118). At Day 43, geometric mean fold increases (GMFI) were 13.7 for the 18-64 cohort and 10.2 for the ≥65 cohort. HI seroconversion rates were 75.8% (95% CI 66.1-83.8%) for the 18-64 cohort and 71.0% (61.1-79.6%) for the ≥65 cohort. HI titers ≥1:40 were achieved in 75.8% (66.1-83.8%) and 73.0% (63.2-81.4%) of participants, respectively. MN seroconversion rates were 80.6% (68.6-89.6%) and 70.0% (56.8-81.2%), while MN titers ≥1:40 were 83.9% (72.3-92.0%) and 86.7% (75.4-94.1%), respectively. No notable differences in immune responses by poultry worker status were observed. Most solicited AEs were mild or moderate, resolving within 3 days.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that two priming doses of the MF59-adjuvanted cell-based H5N8 vaccine induce robust immune responses in both age groups, with no significant differences in efficacy by poultry worker status.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide important data for the development and implementation of vaccines against H5N8 influenza, supporting their use as a public health intervention in at-risk populations.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on healthy adults and the absence of long-term follow-up. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on a single trial with no additional comparative data.

papers.title_zh: MF59 佐剂的基于细胞的 H5N8 流感 疫苗 在 18 岁以上健康人群中两次启动剂量的免疫原性和安全性
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Increased transmission of avian influenza from animals to humans has elevated the risk of an H5 pandemic. METHODS: This phase 2, randomized, observer-blind, multi-center trial assessed the immunogenicity and safety of homologous priming with an MF59-adjuvanted, cell-based H5N8 A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 clade 2.3.4.4b vaccine (aH5N8c). We enrolled adults age ≥18 years, equally stratified into 18-64 (including a poultry-worker subset) and ≥65 year cohorts. Primary and secondary outcomes were homologous antibody responses against H5N8 measured in all participants by hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and in a subset by microneutralization (MN) assays on Days 1, 22, and 43. Solicited adverse events (AEs) were monitored for 7 days post-vaccination, with unsolicited AEs tracked throughout Day 43. RESULTS: 239 participants were vaccinated (18-64 years, n = 121; ≥65 years, n = 118). At Day 43 (21 days post second aH5N8c dose), geometric mean fold increases (GMFI) were 13.7 for the 18-64 cohort and 10.2 for the ≥65 cohort. HI seroconversion rates were 75.8% (95% CI 66.1-83.8%) for the 18-64 cohort and 71.0% (61.1-79.6%) for the ≥65 cohort. HI titers ≥1:40 were achieved in 75.8% (66.1-83.8%) and 73.0% (63.2-81.4%) of participants, respectively. MN seroconversion rates were 80.6% (68.6-89.6%) and 70.0% (56.8-81.2%), while MN titers ≥1:40 were 83.9% (72.3-92.0%) and 86.7% (75.4-94.1%), respectively. No notable differences in immune responses by poultry worker status were observed. Most solicited AEs were mild or moderate, resolving within 3 days. Unsolicited AEs were reported by 16.7% participants by Day 43. CONCLUSION: These data support the use of the MF59-adjuvanted, cell-based monovalent H5N8 vaccine as a public health intervention against H5 influenza.

papers.title: Characterising the longer-term impacts of highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks prior to 2020 on wild bird populations
papers.abstract: Since 2020, there has been a global escalation of the impacts of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) on wild bird species. However, the population-level consequences of this disease remain poorly understood, despite repeated outbreaks affecting wild birds over the past two decades. To address this, we collated population counts and mortality data from 40 historical cases where HPAI mass-mortality occurred in wild bird populations prior to 2020. We characterised local impacts of these outbreaks based on i) initial change in population count from the last count pre-outbreak to the first count post-outbreak, ii) longer-term change in average population counts, iii) change in population trend, and iv) time taken to recover to the pre-outbreak baseline. Following outbreaks, initial population count declines were observed in most cases, with a median decrease of 17% (Inter-quartile range −35% to 5%). Yet in the longer-term, significant reductions in average population counts were detected in only eight of the 40 cases, and a significant decrease in population trend in only two cases. Overall, in the majority of local populations, outbreaks resulted in either limited impacts on population counts or short-term reductions followed by recovery. However, in 25% of cases (10/40) initial declines were not recovered within the monitoring period (4–17 years after the initial outbreak). Initial declines were more apparent in gulls and terns; however, impacts were seen in local populations across a range of taxa. Given that the scale of impacts of HPAI has changed dramatically since 2020, our findings support the need for disease surveillance to be combined with effective population monitoring in order to identify species impacted from the ongoing outbreaks. Further research is also needed to identify strategies for minimising impacts of HPAI, and to understand factors limiting recovery in affected populations.

papers.abstract_zh: 自 2020 年以来,高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 对 野生鸟类 物种的影响在全球范围内不断升级。然而,尽管 暴发 在过去二十年中反复影响 野生鸟类,但人们对这种疾病在人群层面的后果仍知之甚少。为了解决这个问题,我们整理了 2020 年之前 野生鸟类 人群中发生 HPAI 大规模 死亡率 的 40 个历史病例的人口计数和 死亡率 数据。我们根据 i) 从 暴发 之前的最后一次计数到 暴发 后的第一次计数的人口计数初始变化,ii) 长期来描述这些 暴发 的局部影响平均人口数量的变化,iii) 人口趋势的变化,以及 iv) 恢复到 暴发 之前基线所需的时间。暴发 后,大多数情况下观察到初始种群数量下降,中位下降 17%(四分位数范围 -35% 至 5%)。然而从长远来看,40 个案例中只有 8 个案例发现平均人口数量显着减少,只有 2 个案例人口趋势显着下降。总体而言,暴发 对大多数当地人口造成的影响要么是对人口数量的有限影响,要么是短期减少后又恢复。然而,在 25% 的病例 (10/40) 中,初始下降在监测期内(初始 暴发 后 4-17 年)并未恢复。海鸥和燕鸥最初的下降更为明显。然而,对当地居民的一系列分类单元都产生了影响。鉴于自 2020 年以来 HPAI 的影响规模发生了巨大变化,我们的研究结果支持需要将疾病 暴发 与有效的种群监测相结合,以便识别受正在进行的 暴发 影响的物种。还需要进一步研究来确定尽量减少高致病性禽流感影响的策略,并了解限制受影响人群恢复的因素。

papers.title: Emerging Technologies and Artificial Intelligence for Avian Influenza: Transmission Dynamics, Interspecies Spread, and Early Warning
papers.abstract: Avian influenza remains a major global threat. It causes recurring outbreaks, economic losses, and public health concerns. Avian influenza virus (AIV) circulates naturally in wild waterfowl. Recent outbreaks have raised concerns about viral evolution and cross-species transmission. Infections in mammals, including dairy cattle and humans, highlight the need for stronger surveillance. This integrative narrative review examines AIV epidemiology, viral evolution, host adaptation, and transmission pathways. It gives particular attention to dust and aerosol exposure. It also considers interactions among wild birds, poultry, and mammals. Structured searches of PubMed and Scopus covered the literature from January 2015 to 12 December 2025. Selected 2026 publications provided additional context. The review synthesizes scientific studies, outbreak investigations, and epidemiological reports. It also examines conventional diagnostics and emerging artificial intelligence (AI), molecular, and sensor-based technologies. Current surveillance and biosecurity approaches face challenges in early detection and coordinated response across production settings. AI-enabled monitoring and advanced diagnostics may improve risk assessment, early warning, and outbreak management. However, these technologies require further field validation. Stronger integration of environmental monitoring, data sharing, and established biosecurity practices is needed. A One Health approach can connect animal, human, and environmental surveillance. Such integration may strengthen AIV preparedness and reduce future outbreak risks.

papers.title: Factors influencing the timeliness of reporting highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks in Europe
papers.abstract: Timely reporting of zoonotic infectious diseases allows for rapid response and mitigation by health authorities. However, little is known about the factors influencing the timeliness of disease outbreak reports. The World Animal Health Information System provides extensive data on delays that arise between first suspecting and subsequently reporting outbreaks of notifiable animal diseases. Here we analysed these report delays using a Bayesian semi-parametric survival model, to assess socio-demographic, epidemiological and cultural covariates on the timeliness of disease outbreak reports in Europe, using highly pathogenic avian influenza as a model disease. The survival model included time-varying coefficients and a penalized spline to account for temporal fluctuations in reporting rates, and parsimonious shrinkage (Bayesian model selection) was obtained using Dirichlet-Laplace priors. The results indicated that outbreaks occurring in wild birds, high outbreak notification rates, country, day of week and national holidays were all associated with delayed outbreak reporting times. Higher political stability and better corruption control, as defined by the World Bank, were also associated with longer reporting times, while high per capita gross national income and local poultry density were associated with shorter reporting delays. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 及时报告人畜共患传染病可以让卫生当局快速做​​出反应并缓解病情。然而,对于影响疾病暴发报告及时性的因素却知之甚少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用贝叶斯半参数生存模型分析了报告延迟,重点关注欧洲疾病 暴发 报告及时性的社会人口统计学、流行病学和文化协变量,并使用 高致病性禽流感 作为模型疾病。
elements_zh.methods: 生存模型包括时变系数和惩罚样条,以解释报告率的时间波动,并使用狄利克雷-拉普拉斯先验获得简约收缩(贝叶斯模型选择)。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,暴发 发生在 野生鸟类、高 暴发 通知率、国家、星期几和国定假日都与延迟的 暴发 报告时间相关。根据世界银行的定义,较高的政治稳定性和更好的腐败控制也与较长的报告时间相关,而较高的人均国民总收入和当地家禽密度则与较短的报告延迟相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强调了影响 暴发 报告及时性的因素之间复杂的相互作用,其新颖之处在于贝叶斯半参数生存模型在此背景下的应用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果还可能有助于为卫生当局提供量身定制的、针对特定国家的建议,并通过国际卫生组织秘密提供,以改善疾病报告。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计的具体局限性,但贝叶斯半参数生存模型的使用表明研究结果具有中等程度的可信度。

papers.title: Genetic diversity of H5 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses detected in Laos, 2019–2024: multiple clades, subtypes, and genotypes
papers.abstract: Since 2004, H5 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) from several clades have caused outbreaks in Laos, with clade 2.3.2.1e H5N1 viruses predominating since 2015. However, genomic data on H5 HPAIVs circulating in Laos after 2018 remain limited. In this study, we performed whole-genome sequencing of 37 H5Nx HPAIVs isolated in Laos during 2019–2024 and investigated their genetic characteristics using phylogenetic analyses alongside publicly available Lao HPAIV sequences collected during 2015–2024. Based on gene constellations, 12 genotypes were identified across three HA clades: seven clade 2.3.2.1e genotypes (E1–E7), three clade 2.3.4.4b genotypes (B1–B3), and two clade 2.3.4.4h genotypes (H1–H2). Clade 2.3.2.1e H5N1 viruses predominated overall, and novel genotypes emerged through reassortment with 2.3.4.4b H5N1 and Eurasian low-pathogenicity avian influenza (LPAI) viruses. In contrast, 2.3.4.4b H5Nx and 2.3.4.4h H5N6 viruses were detected sporadically. Genetically related 2.3.2.1e H5N1 genotypes co-circulated in Laos, Cambodia, and Vietnam. Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses detected in 2023 clustered with viruses detected in East Asia and North America since 2021. Genotype H2, a 2.3.4.4h H5N6 virus, was genetically similar to H5N6 viruses epidemiologically linked to a human infection in Laos and detected in poultry and humans in China. In addition, genotype E7 was continuously detected from 2022 to 2024 and had the same gene constellation as viruses associated with human and mammalian infections in Cambodia and Vietnam. These findings demonstrate persistent circulation and reassortment of H5 HPAIVs in Laos, highlighting the need for genomic surveillance to monitor zoonotic risk and transboundary transmission in Southeast Asia.

papers.title: Antiviral Treatment of Human Influenza A(H5N1) Infection: Treatment Timing, Clinical Outcomes, Virological Outcomes, and Antiviral Resistance: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Human influenza A(H5N1) infection remains a clinically important zoonotic disease, but evidence on antiviral effectiveness is limited by observational designs, heterogeneous treatment timing, and potentially overlapping patient populations. This systematic review synthesized evidence on antiviral regimens, treatment timing, clinical and virological outcomes, and antiviral resistance in laboratory-confirmed human A(H5N1) infection. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect was conducted from database inception to 1 July 2026. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale and the JBI Case Series Checklist. The clinical and methodological characteristics varied across studies; consequently, the findings were synthesized narratively. Potential population overlap was considered when synthesizing findings across publications to avoid duplicate aggregation of patient data. Of 2,329 records identified, 22 publications were included. Oseltamivir treatment was associated with a lower hazard of death than no documented anti-influenza antiviral treatment (adjusted hazard ratio 0.51, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.77). Treatment within 2 days showed lower odds of death, although the overall estimate was not statistically significant (adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% confidence interval 0.03–1.04). Among patients without respiratory failure at treatment initiation, earlier treatment was associated with lower mortality (adjusted odds ratio 0.17, 95% confidence interval 0.03–0.89). Evidence for other antivirals was limited, and one confirmed treatment-emergent H274Y neuraminidase resistance event was identified. Overall, oseltamivir, particularly when initiated early and before advanced respiratory failure, was associated with improved clinical outcomes, although causal inference remains limited by confounding, heterogeneity, and potentially overlapping study populations.

papers.title: Naturally Occurring PB2 Paired Substitutions Confer Host-Dependent Polymerase Phenotypes in H7N9 Avian Influenza Viruses with Differential ANP32 Support
papers.abstract: H7N9 avian influenza viruses have caused repeated human infections since 2013, but the effects of naturally occurring PB2 substitution combinations on polymerase activity remain poorly understood. We analyzed 899 avian-derived and 1087 human-derived H7N9 PB2 sequences collected between 2013 and 2025. Six PB2 positions (109, 122, 191, 340, 559, and 640) showed distinct frequency changes across epidemic waves and host origins. Pairwise analysis identified five representative combinations with different temporal patterns. In minigenome assays, four paired substitutions reduced polymerase activity in human 293T cells at both 33 °C and 37 °C, whereas none of the five significantly altered activity in chicken DF1 cells at 37 °C or 41 °C. Several paired substitutions showed polymerase activity profiles different from those of the corresponding single substitutions in the tested cellular assays. ANP32 overexpression experiments showed different polymerase activity responses across the tested cellular conditions. Under chicken ANP32A expression, none of the paired-substitution polymerases differed significantly from the wild type, whereas human ANP32A and ANP32B overexpression did not enhance their activity in DF1 cells. Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed detectable interactions between PB2 variants and human or chicken ANP32 proteins. Structural modeling further revealed differences in predicted PB2–ANP32A interfaces among the tested variants. Together, these results show that the tested PB2 substitution combinations produced different polymerase activity profiles in human 293T and chicken DF1 cells and exhibited different responses to ANP32 overexpression under the examined conditions. The findings provide insight into the functional consequences of PB2 evolution during H7N9 circulation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effects of naturally occurring PB2 substitution combinations on polymerase activity in H7N9 avian influenza viruses. The research focuses on understanding how these substitutions influence viral replication in human and chicken cells. By analyzing 899 avian-derived and 1087 human-derived PB2 sequences collected between 2013 and 2025, the study identifies six PB2 positions with distinct frequency changes across epidemic waves and host origins. The findings reveal that certain paired substitutions reduce polymerase activity in human 293T cells but do not significantly alter activity in chicken DF1 cells. Additionally, the study shows that polymerase activity profiles differ between paired and single substitutions in cellular assays. ANP32 overexpression experiments further demonstrate varied responses across cellular conditions. These results provide insight into the functional consequences of PB2 evolution during H7N9 circulation, highlighting the importance of host-specific factors in viral polymerase activity. However, the study notes that human ANP32A and ANP32B overexpression did not enhance polymerase activity in DF1 cells, suggesting limitations in generalizing findings to other hosts.

Volume 32, Number 12—December 2026 Research Letter Serologic Evidence of Avian Influenza Virus Exposure in Livestock, Egypt, 2024–2026 Suggested citation for this article Abstract Spillover of influenza A(H5N1) virus to cattle in the United States sparked global concern. We investigated whether endemic avian influenza viruses are potentially spilling over into domestic livestock in Egypt. We detected influenza H9N2 antibodies in 2.5% and H5N1 antibodies in 2.9%–4.5% of tested animals. Additional surveillance will elucidate host infection dynamics. The emergence of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b virus in dairy cattle in the United States represented a major shift in influenza virus ecology, marking the first sustained transmission of H5N1 virus in a mammalian livestock species (1). Genotype B3.13 was reported in dairy cows in early 2024 in several US states; data indicated a spillover event from wild birds to cattle and then interstate transmission through cow movement (1). A defining feature of H5N1 virus infection in dairy cattle is its marked tropism for the mammary gland, resulting in extremely high viral titers in milk and relatively lower viral loads in respiratory samples (2). Mechanical transmission via the milking process is believed to play a major role in cow-to-cow transmission, particularly in large dairy operations. Cow infection was not limited to genotype B3.13; European genotype euDG was shown to be able to cause infection in an experimental setting (3), and North American genotype D1.1 was detected in cattle in the United States (3). Infection of other livestock species, including goats, sheep, swine, and alpacas, was reported in mixed-species backyards and farms in the United States and United Kingdom (4,5). In 2026, a farm in the Netherlands had a cat infected with H5N1 virus; a cow at that farm had antibodies against the virus (6). Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus and low-pathogenicity avian influenza A(H9N2) virus are widely and endemically circulating in poultry in Egypt on farms and backyards and at live bird markets (7). Subtype H5N1 was detected in feral rats in poultry production areas (8). In addition, reassortment events between the H5N1 and H9N2 subtypes led to the emergence of novel clade 2.3.4.4b influenza A(H5N2) viruses (9). To determine whether those viruses are spilling over to livestock in Egypt, particularly in mixed-species settings, we conducted a serosurveillance study in northern Egypt. During October 2024–January 2026, we collected 444 serum samples from 33 conveniently selected small farms (≈10 cattle, no mixed species) and backyards housing cattle (1–3 cattle with mixed species) in 3 governorates (n = 155, n = 59, and n = 230) in northern Egypt, representing common practices in Egypt. Sheep and goats were also sampled if housed in the same backyards as cattle. All sampled animals were apparently healthy adults. We tested serum samples for antibodies against a 2025 Egyptian clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 (A/duck/Egypt/BA20361C/2022) virus using hemagglutination inhibition (HI) and microneutralization (MN) assays and against a G1-like Egypt influenza A(H9N2) (A/chicken/Egypt/RA20191OP/2022) virus by HI in accordance with World Health Organization protocols (10). We considered an antibody titer >1:40 as positive for both assays. Data on the number of cows, presence of other mammals (e.g., donkeys and horses), and presence of avian species (poultry and/or wild birds) were available for 271 samples. We performed statistical comparisons with χ2 or Fisher exact tests; we considered p<0.05 statistically significant. Overall, 11 (2.5%) serum specimens tested positive for influenza A(H9N2) antibodies, 20 (4.5%) were positive for influenza A(H5N1) antibodies by HI, and 13 (2.9%) were positive for influenza A(H5N1) antibodies by MN (Figure, panel A). Positive titers were 40–160 (Figure, panel B). None of the samples tested positive for antibodies against both viruses. Of the 20 H5N1 virus specimens positive by HI, 12 tested positive by MN; 1 specimen was negative by HI and positive by MN. All influenza H9N2-positive specimens were from 3 locations in the same governorate (p = 0.005). Influenza A(H5N1) antibodies were detected in 2 governorates; the differences in detection rates by governorate were statistically significant (0%, 1.3%, and 4.8%; p = 0.049). All H5N1 virus–seropositive specimens were from cattle (Table). We detected H9N2 antibodies in 6/374 (1.6%) of cattle specimens, 1/31 (3.2%) of goat specimens, and 4/39 (10.3%) of sheep specimens (p = 0.004). Presence of other animals did not predict seropositivity. Small farms had a significantly higher proportion of H5N1 virus–positive animals tested by MN (p = 0.039). Our findings indicate that spillover of avian influenza viruses to cattle and other livestock is not geographically restricted or caused by certain genotypes of H5N1 virus. Clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus of the EA-2021-AB genotype and G1-like H9N2 virus appear to be spilling over into livestock in Egypt; however, because our evidence is serologic, we could not ascertain whether true infection is occurring and whether the same signs seen in the United States are common in cattle in Egypt. Even so, the evidence is a strong indicator that spillover is occurring, similar to that reported in Europe (4,6). Furthermore, spillover is not restricted to cattle; some sheep and goats tested in our study were seropositive for influenza A(H9N2) virus. Surveillance for avian influenza viruses in Egypt and other countries, especially those in which avian influenza is endemic, will verify infection and provide data on frequency, routes of transmission, and factors affecting infection of and transmission to livestock. Dr. Gomaa is a virologist at the National Research Centre, Giza, and a member of the Center of Scientific Excellence for virus research. His work focuses on emerging and reemerging viruses, avian influenza, coronaviruses, vaccine development, viral immunology, and pandemic preparedness. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether endemic avian influenza viruses are spilling over into domestic livestock in Egypt, following global concern over the spillover of influenza A(H5N1) virus to cattle in the United States.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A serosurveillance study was conducted in northern Egypt from October 2024 to January 2026, collecting 444 serum samples from 33 small farms and backyards across three governorates, representing common livestock practices in Egypt.
analysis.methods: To determine whether avian influenza viruses are spilling over to livestock in Egypt, the researchers conducted a serosurveillance study in northern Egypt, collecting serum samples from cattle in small farms and backyards.
analysis.main_results: Influenza H9N2 antibodies were detected in 2.5% of tested animals, while H5N1 antibodies were found in 2.9%–4.5% of the animals.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that avian influenza viruses may be spilling over into livestock in Egypt, highlighting the need for further surveillance to understand host infection dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the importance of monitoring avian influenza virus exposure in livestock to better understand transmission patterns and potential zoonotic risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to small farms and backyards with no mixed species, and the evidence is based on serologic detection, which may not fully capture the extent of viral transmission.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the spillover of avian influenza viruses into domestic livestock in Egypt. Researchers conducted a serosurveillance study in northern Egypt from October 2024 to January 2026, collecting serum samples from 33 small farms and backyards across three governorates. They detected H9N2 antibodies in 2.5% of tested animals and H5N1 antibodies in 2.9%–4.5% of the animals. These findings suggest that avian influenza viruses may be spilling over into livestock in Egypt, emphasizing the need for additional surveillance to understand host infection dynamics. The study was limited to small farms and backyards with no mixed species, and the evidence is based on serologic detection, which may not fully capture the extent of viral transmission. The results have implications for monitoring avian influenza virus exposure in livestock to better understand transmission patterns and potential zoonotic risks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查地方性 禽流感 病毒是否正在蔓延到埃及的家畜中,继全球对美国牛感染 A (H5N1) 流感病毒 跨物种溢出 的担忧之后。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 10 月至 2026 年 1 月在埃及北部进行了一项血清监测研究,从三个省的 33 个小农场和后院收集了 444 份血清样本,代表了埃及常见的畜牧业做法。
elements_zh.methods: 为了确定 禽流感 病毒是否蔓延到埃及的牲畜身上,研究人员在埃及北部进行了一项血清监测研究,从小型农场和后院的牛身上收集了血清样本。
elements_zh.main_results: 2.5%的测试动物检测到H9N2流感抗体,2.9%–4.5%的动物检测到H5N1流感抗体。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,禽流感 病毒可能正在扩散到埃及的牲畜中,这凸显了需要进一步使用 监测 来了解 宿主 感染动态。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明监测牲畜中 禽流感 病毒暴露的重要性,以更好地了解 传播 模式和潜在的人畜共患病风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于没有混合物种的小农场和后院,证据基于血清学检测,可能无法完全掌握病毒 传播 的范围。

papers.title: Rare recovery of reassortants between contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses and human influenza A viruses in vitro
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) pandemics can arise when animal-derived and human-adapted IAVs exchange genome segments; however, whether contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses can generate viable reassortants with human IAVs is unclear. Here, we tested the reassortment potential of two clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses with human-adapted H1N1 and H3N2 IAVs using a biosafe reassortment system. Across multiple coinfection conditions, we genotyped 2,698 plaque-purified viral clones and recovered 20 reassortants (0.74%). Polymerase assays identified human IAV subunits, particularly H1N1 PA or H3N2 PB2, that increased H5N1 polymerase activity. Thus, contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses can reassort with human IAVs, but factors beyond polymerase compatibility may limit their recovery.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

papers.title: EVALUATING THE INTERACTION BETWEEN INACTIVATED AVIAN INFLUENZA (H9N2) AND NEWCASTLE DISEASE-INFECTIOUS BRONCHITIS VACCINES IN BROILERS
papers.abstract: This study evaluated how inactivated Newcastle disease (ND) and H9N2 avian influenza (AI) vaccines modify immune responses generated under a live ND-infectious bronchitis (IB) vaccination program in broiler chickens. A total of 150 Ross 308 chicks were assigned to 5 groups. Vaccinated groups received the live respiratory program and differed in their inactivated vaccine exposure: no inactivated vaccine, inactivated ND vaccine, inactivated H9N2 vaccine, or a bivalent inactivated ND-H9N2 vaccine; an unvaccinated group served as the control. Humoral responses were assessed by ELISA and hemagglutination-inhibition assays, cellular responses were evaluated using selected cytokines, and body weight and lymphoid organ indices were monitored. AI ELISA responses showed significant effects of group, age, and their interaction, with the strongest responses occurring in H9N2-vaccinated groups. ND and IB ELISA responses also varied with age and vaccination program, whereas HI testing provided less separation among groups. Cytokine responses were dynamic and age dependent; IL-4 and IL-10 patterns indicated treatment-related Th2/regulatory activity at selected ages, while Th1-associated cytokines showed variable responses. Growth and thymus indices differed among treatments or ages, whereas bursa and spleen indices were less discriminatory. Overall, concurrent inactivated vaccine exposure altered the magnitude and timing of immune responses generated alongside the live ND-IB program, indicating that antigen combination and vaccination timing should be considered when designing broiler vaccination schedules.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how inactivated Newcastle disease (ND) and H9N2 avian influenza (AI) vaccines affect immune responses in broiler chickens that are also receiving a live ND-infectious bronchitis (IB) vaccination program. The research involved 150 Ross 308 chicks divided into five groups, with varying exposure to inactivated vaccines. Humoral and cellular immune responses were measured using ELISA, hemagglutination-inhibition assays, and cytokine analysis. Results showed that H9N2-vaccinated groups had the strongest AI ELISA responses, while ND and IB responses varied with age and vaccination program. Cytokine patterns indicated Th2/regulatory activity in some groups. The study suggests that antigen combination and vaccination timing should be considered in broiler vaccination schedules. However, the findings are limited by the controlled experimental design and lack of long-term follow-up, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis_zh.methods: 通过 ELISA 和血凝抑制测定评估体液反应,使用选定的细胞因子评估细胞反应,并监测体重和淋巴器官指数。
analysis_zh.main_results: AI ELISA 反应显示出群体、年龄及其相互作用的显着影响,其中最强的反应发生在 H9N2 疫苗接种组中。ND 和 IB ELISA 反应也随年龄和 疫苗接种 程序而变化,而 HI 测试提供的组间分离较少。细胞因子反应是动态的且依赖于年龄;IL-4 和 IL-10 模式表明 治疗 相关的 Th2/调节活性在选定的年龄,而 Th1 相关细胞因子则表现出不同的反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,同时灭活的 疫苗 暴露改变了与实时 ND-IB 程序一起产生的 免疫应答 的幅度和时间,表明在设计肉鸡 疫苗接种 时间表时应考虑抗原组合和 疫苗接种 时间。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,灭活的 疫苗 与活的 ND-IB 程序的组合可能会影响肉鸡中的 免疫应答,这可以为开发更有效的 疫苗接种 控制 禽流感 策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于受控实验设计,组数和年龄点数量有限,这可能会限制普遍性。由于缺乏长期随访和潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Operationalising Cross-Sectoral One Health Event-Based Surveillance in Albania: A Six-Year Case Study of the Integrated Surveillance Information System
papers.abstract: One Health surveillance requires that information from one sector triggers assessment and action in another. This descriptive case study examines how Albania’s Integrated Surveillance Information System (SISI) operationalised cross-sectoral event-based surveillance (EBS) and what limited routine interoperability, using governance documents, the EBS register of April 2020 to August 2026 and staff surveys. The register held 399 signals, 93 of them animal-health or suspected zoonotic events. Of 363 completed verifications, 255 (70.2%) were substantiated and 41 had a recorded escalation to case notification or outbreak investigation. Veterinary services initiated 26 signals, 20 of 23 with dates registered within two days. After one veterinary brucellosis signal, contact investigation found two confirmed human infections within six days, and avian influenza A(H5N1) signals led to testing of 60 exposed persons, all negative. Human anthrax and brucellosis events were signalled to veterinary services, with an animal source identified in two. Integration was operational at the event level, through reciprocal-signalling rules, shared event records and defined field responsibilities. Routine data remained unjoined, since the veterinary system was unlinked, animal-side actions were unevenly documented, community participation declined and cybersecurity constrained interfaces. Event-level integration can offer a transferable starting point where routine data systems cannot yet be joined.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore how Albania's Integrated Surveillance Information System operationalised cross-sectoral event-based surveillance for avian influenza A viruses and to identify factors limiting routine interoperability between sectors.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive case study was conducted in Albania from April 2020 to August 2026, examining the Integrated Surveillance Information System (SISI) and its implementation across sectors. The study included governance documents, an event register, and staff surveys to assess the system's functionality and challenges.
analysis.methods: The study utilised governance documents, an event register spanning April 2020 to August 2026, and staff surveys to evaluate the operationalisation of cross-sectoral event-based surveillance. It focused on the integration of signals between veterinary and human health sectors.
analysis.main_results: Of 363 completed verifications, 255 (70.2%) were substantiated, and 41 had a recorded escalation to case notification or outbreak investigation. Veterinary services initiated 26 signals, 20 of which were registered within two days.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that event-level integration can function effectively as a starting point for cross-sectoral surveillance, even when routine data systems are not fully interoperable.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides insights into the operational feasibility of event-based surveillance systems for avian influenza, offering a model for improving cross-sectoral coordination in public health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on existing records and staff surveys, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on descriptive analysis rather than experimental or longitudinal data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates how Albania's Integrated Surveillance Information System (SISI) operationalised cross-sectoral event-based surveillance for avian influenza A viruses. It highlights the system's ability to trigger assessments and actions across sectors, with 70.2% of 363 completed verifications being substantiated. The research demonstrates that event-level integration can serve as a practical starting point for surveillance, even when routine data systems are not fully interoperable. However, the study is limited by its descriptive nature and reliance on existing records, which may affect the strength of its conclusions. The findings suggest that such systems can enhance public health preparedness by improving coordination between veterinary and human health sectors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨阿尔巴尼亚的综合 监测 信息系统如何针对 禽流感 A 病毒操作基于跨部门事件的 监测,并确定限制部门之间常规互操作性的因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2020 年 4 月至 2026 年 8 月在阿尔巴尼亚进行了一项描述性案例研究,研究了综合 监测 信息系统 (SISI) 及其跨部门的实施情况。该研究包括治理文件、事件登记册和员工调查,以评估系统的功能和挑战。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究利用治理文件、2020 年 4 月至 2026 年 8 月的事件登记册以及员工调查来评估基于跨部门事件的 监测 的运作情况。它的重点是兽医和人类健康部门之间的信号整合。
elements_zh.main_results: 在完成的 363 项核查中,255 项 (70.2%) 得到证实,41 项已升级为案件通知或 暴发 调查。兽医部门发出了 26 条信号,其中 20 条在两天内得到登记。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,即使常规数据系统不完全可互操作,事件级集成也可以作为跨部门 监测 的起点有效发挥作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究深入探讨了 禽流感 基于事件的 监测 系统的运营可行性,为改善公共卫生领域的跨部门协调提供了模型。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖现有记录和员工调查而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差。证据是中等的,因为它是基于描述性分析而不是实验或纵向数据。

papers.abstract_zh: One Health 监测 要求来自一个部门的信息触发另一部门的评估和行动。这项描述性案例研究利用治理文件、2020 年 4 月至 2026 年 8 月的 EBS 登记册和员工调查,探讨了阿尔巴尼亚的综合 监测 信息系统 (SISI) 如何操作基于事件的跨部门 监测 (EBS) 以及哪些限制了常规互操作性。该登记册包含 399 个信号,其中 93 个与动物健康或疑似人畜共患事件有关。在 363 项已完成的核查中,255 项 (70.2%) 得到证实,41 项已记录升级为病例通知或 暴发 调查。兽医部门发出了 26 个信号,其中 23 个中的 20 个信号在两天内登记了日期。在收到一份兽医布鲁氏菌病信号后,接触调查在六天内发现了两例确诊的人类感染病例,禽流感 A(H5N1) 信号导致对 60 名暴露者进行了检测,结果均为阴性。人类炭疽和布鲁氏菌病事件已向兽医部门发出信号,其中两个动物源已被确定。通过互惠信号规则、共享事件记录和定义的现场职责,集成在事件级别上进行。常规数据仍然没有连接,因为兽医系统没有联系,动物方面的行动记录不均匀,社区参与度下降,网络安全接口受到限制。事件级集成可以提供一个可转移的起点,其中常规数据系统尚无法连接。

analysis_zh.main_results: 在完成的 363 项核查中,255 项 (70.2%) 得到证实,41 项已升级为案件通知或 暴发 调查。兽医部门发出了 26 条信号,其中 20 条在两天内得到登记。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,即使常规数据系统不完全可互操作,事件级集成也可以作为跨部门 监测 的起点有效发挥作用。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to report the whole-genome sequences of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza viruses detected in felines in Bangladesh during 2025–2026, highlighting the potential for cross-species transmission and the need to understand viral evolution in non-traditional hosts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the collection and analysis of whole-genome sequences from three highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza viruses isolated from cats in Bangladesh between 2025 and 2026. These isolates were compared phylogenetically to other known strains.
analysis.methods: The researchers obtained whole-genome sequences of the H5N1 viruses from infected cats and performed phylogenetic analysis to classify the strains into clades. They also identified mutations in key polymerase and HA markers associated with mammalian adaptation and virulence.
analysis.main_results: Two of the strains grouped within clade 2.3.2.1a, while the third was classified within clade 2.3.4.4b. The isolates were found to harbor mutations in key polymerase and HA markers linked to mammalian adaptation and virulence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that H5N1 avian influenza viruses can infect and replicate in felines, potentially indicating a broader host range than previously recognized. This adds to the understanding of viral evolution and cross-species transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results contribute to the surveillance of H5N1 in non-traditional hosts, which is critical for assessing the risk of zoonotic transmission and for developing targeted diagnostic and control strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level reporting and does not include detailed experimental or clinical data. The evidence is moderate as it is based on phylogenetic classification and mutation analysis without further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports the whole-genome sequences of three highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza viruses detected in cats in Bangladesh during 2025–2026. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that two strains grouped within clade 2.3.2.1a, while the third was classified within clade 2.3.4.4b. The isolates exhibited mutations in key polymerase and HA markers associated with mammalian adaptation and virulence. These findings highlight the potential for H5N1 to infect non-traditional hosts like felines, contributing to the understanding of viral evolution and cross-species transmission. The study provides important insights for surveillance and risk assessment but is limited to abstract-level reporting without detailed experimental or clinical data, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.title_original: Nano-Sized Water-in-Oil-in-Water Emulsion with Lipopolysaccharide Enhancement Improves Immunogenicity and Accelerates the Decline of Viral Shedding in an Inactivated H5N1 (Clade 2.3.4.4b) Poultry Vaccine

analysis.research_question_and_background: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b continues to spread globally, and conventional water-in-oil (W/O) emulsion-adjuvanted inactivated poultry vaccines show inconsistent immunogenicity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated three formulations—a nano-sized water-in-oil-in-water (W/O/W) emulsion, an LPS-enhanced W/O/W emulsion, and a conventional W/O emulsion (Montanide ISA 71)—in specific-pathogen-free (SPF) chickens.
analysis.methods: The formulations were characterized physicochemically and tested for hemagglutination-inhibition (HI) titers, IFN-γ and IL-6 expression, and protection after homologous challenge. Survival was compared using Kaplan–Meier analysis with the log-rank test, and viral shedding was assessed by RT-PCR and embryonated-egg passage.
analysis.main_results: The W/O/W emulsion was smaller (241 vs. 1095 nm) and less viscous than the conventional emulsion (both p < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that reducing emulsion particle size and adding LPS may enhance vaccine performance by improving immunogenicity and accelerating the decline of viral shedding.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results may inform the development of more effective inactivated H5N1 vaccines for poultry, potentially improving disease control and reducing viral spread.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to SPF chickens and does not report human outcomes, but the evidence is strong due to direct comparison of formulations and clear statistical analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether reducing emulsion particle size and adding lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to an inactivated H5N1 (clade 2.3.4.4b) poultry vaccine improves immunogenicity and accelerates the decline of viral shedding. The research aimed to address the inconsistent performance of conventional water-in-oil (W/O) emulsion-adjuvanted vaccines against HPAI H5N1. Three formulations were tested in specific-pathogen-free (SPF) chickens: a nano-sized water-in-oil-in-water (W/O/W) emulsion, an LPS-enhanced W/O/W emulsion, and a conventional W/O emulsion. The nano-sized emulsion was found to be smaller and less viscous than the conventional one, with statistically significant differences (p < 0.05). The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the modified emulsions may enhance vaccine performance. The results could have implications for improving poultry vaccine efficacy against H5N1. papers.title: Etiopathological Study of Colisepticemia with Coinfection of Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza and Mycoplasma in Broilers
papers.abstract: The present study was conducted to detect Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza (LPAI) and Mycoplasma in 30 broiler flocks (5 birds per flock) showing gross lesions of colisepticemia (Fibrinous pericarditis and perihepatitis) without any significant gross lesion in trachea and bronchi. The study comprised of flock wise mortality, gross and histopathological examination of colisepticemia and molecular identification from pooled sample of trachea for the presence of E. coli, LPAI, Mycoplasma gallisepticum and Mycoplasma synoviae. The mortality among 30 flocks varied between 0.32 and 6.75% with an average of 1.89%. Gross and histopathological lesions were predominantly found in liver, heart, spleen and lungs. All the 30 flocks were found positive for phoA gene of E. coli, whereas 5 (16.60%), 9 (30%) and 4 (13.30%) flocks were positive for H9N2 subtype of Avian influenza virus, i.e. LPAI, Mycoplasma gallisepticum and Mycoplasma synoviae, respectively. Findings of the present study confirmed the concurrent infection of colisepticemia with other primary pathogens such as LPAI, M. gallisepticum and M. synoviae, which indicate that Escherichia coli is a major secondary opportunistic pathogen in a respiratory disease complex of chicken.
papers.journal: The Indian journal of veterinary sciences and biotechnology

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对 30 只肉鸡群进行,每群有 5 只鸡,表现出结肠败血症的肉眼病变,特别是纤维蛋白性心包炎和肝周炎,但没有明显的气管或支气管病变。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究涉及群体 死亡率 评估、受影响组织的肉眼和组织病理学检查,以及使用合并的气管样本进行分子鉴定,以检测大肠杆菌、LPAI、鸡毒支原体和滑液支原体。
elements_zh.main_results: 30只鸡群大肠埃希菌phoA基因全部呈阳性,而禽流感病毒H9N2亚型、鸡毒支原体和滑液支原体分别有5只(16.60%)、9只(30%)和4只(13.30%)鸡群呈阳性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证实,大肠杆菌是鸡呼吸道疾病复合体中主要的继发机会致病菌,与 LPAI 和支原体共存。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对肉鸡败血症病因病理学动态的深入了解,强调了监测 禽流感 暴发 中次要病原体的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象水平的报告,证据基于合并样本的分子检测,这可能无法反映个体鸟类的感染情况。证据强度中等。

papers.source_body_en: The present study was conducted to detect Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza (LPAI) and Mycoplasma in 30 broiler flocks (5 birds per flock) showing gross lesions of colisepticemia (Fibrinous pericarditis and perihepatitis) without any significant gross lesion in trachea and bronchi. The study comprised of flock wise mortality, gross and histopathological examination of colisepticemia and molecular identification from pooled sample of trachea for the presence of E. coli, LPAI, Mycoplasma gallisepticum and Mycoplasma synoviae. The mortality among 30 flocks varied between 0.32 and 6.75% with an average of 1.89%. Gross and histopathological lesions were predominantly found in liver, heart, spleen and lungs. All the 30 flocks were found positive for phoA gene of E. coli, whereas 5 (16.60%), 9 (30%) and 4 (13.30%) flocks were positive for H9N2 subtype of Avian influenza virus, i.e. LPAI, Mycoplasma gallisepticum and Mycoplasma synoviae, respectively. Findings of the present study confirmed the concurrent infection of colisepticemia with other primary pathogens such as LPAI, M. gallisepticum and M. synoviae, which indicate that Escherichia coli is a major secondary opportunistic pathogen in a respiratory disease complex of chicken.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查低致病性 禽流感 (LPAI) 与患有结肠败血症的肉鸡支原体感染之间的病因病理学关系,解决了解继发性病原体在呼吸道疾病复合体中的作用的需要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对 30 只肉鸡群进行,每群有 5 只鸡,表现出结肠败血症的肉眼病变,特别是纤维蛋白性心包炎和肝周炎,但没有明显的气管或支气管病变。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究涉及群体 死亡率 评估、受影响组织的肉眼和组织病理学检查,以及使用合并的气管样本进行分子鉴定,以检测大肠杆菌、LPAI、鸡毒支原体和滑液支原体。
analysis_zh.main_results: 30只鸡群大肠埃希菌phoA基因全部呈阳性,而禽流感病毒H9N2亚型、鸡毒支原体和滑液支原体分别有5只(16.60%)、9只(30%)和4只(13.30%)鸡群呈阳性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证实,大肠杆菌是鸡呼吸道疾病复合体中主要的继发机会致病菌,与 LPAI 和支原体共存。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对肉鸡败血症病因病理学动态的深入了解,强调了监测 禽流感 暴发 中次要病原体的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象水平的报告,证据基于合并样本的分子检测,这可能无法反映个体鸟类的感染情况。证据强度中等。

papers.title: Short-term associations between wild-bird and mammalian high pathogenic avian influenza detection in the United States
papers.abstract: High pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) detections in mammals have raised concern about repeated wildlife spillover and the targeting of mammalian surveillance. We evaluated whether wild-bird detection records contained short-term explanatory and predictive information about mammalian detections in the United States. Public surveillance records from April 2022 to July 2026 comprised 18,523 wild-bird and 815 mammalian detections. Monthly state-level mammalian counts were analysed using negative-binomial mixed models adjusted for seasonality, preceding mammalian detections and state-level heterogeneity. The selected model contained contemporaneous and one-month-lagged same-state wild-bird counts. A doubling of one plus the contemporaneous wild-bird count was associated with a 57.9% increase in the expected mammalian count (95% CI 43.5-73.8%), and a doubling of the preceding-month count with a 15.9% increase (5.2-27.8%). Bordering-state exposure did not improve fit. In a six-month temporal holdout, adding same-state wild-bird exposure reduced mean absolute error by 23.8% and root mean squared error by 27.9%, although total detections remained overpredicted. After exact-row deduplication, the corresponding effects were 59.7% and 13.3%. Wild-bird surveillance records contained short-term, geographically local information about mammalian HPAI detection activity, but the associations do not establish direct transmission and require further calibration before operational forecasting.

source_records.abstract: High pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) detections in mammals have raised concern about repeated wildlife spillover and the targeting of mammalian surveillance. We evaluated whether wild-bird detection records contained short-term explanatory and predictive information about mammalian detections in the United States. Public surveillance records from April 2022 to July 2026 comprised 18,523 wild-bird and 815 mammalian detections. Monthly state-level mammalian counts were analysed using negative-binomial mixed models adjusted for seasonality, preceding mammalian detections and state-level heterogeneity. The selected model contained contemporaneous and one-month-lagged same-state wild-bird counts. A doubling of one plus the contemporaneous wild-bird count was associated with a 57.9% increase in the expected mammalian count (95% CI 43.5-73.8%), and a doubling of the preceding-month count with a 15.9% increase (5.2-27.8%). Bordering-state exposure did not improve fit. In a six-month temporal holdout, adding same-state wild-bird exposure reduced mean absolute error by 23.8% and root mean squared error by 27.9%, although total detections remained overpredicted. After exact-row deduplication, the corresponding effects were 59.7% and 13.3%. Wild-bird surveillance records contained short-term, geographically local information about mammalian HPAI detection activity, but the associations do not establish direct transmission and require further calibration before operational forecasting.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,野鸟 传播 记录包含有关哺乳动物 HPAI 检测活动的短期、地理本地信息,但这些关联并未建立直接的 传播,需要进一步校准以进行业务预测。

papers.full_text: Disclaimer: Early release articles are not considered as final versions. Any changes will be reflected in the online version in the month the article is officially released. Volume 32, Number 12—December 2026 Research Letter Cross-Protection against Influenza A(H5) Clade 2.3.4.4b Viruses after A(H1N1)pdm09 Infection Suggested citation for this article Abstract We challenged ferrets previously infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus with H5N1 or H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses to assess cross-protection. Results show that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 virus immunity conferred partial protection against both viruses, with slightly reduced protection against H5N5 compared with H5N1, potentially reflecting the absence of cross-reactive N5 neuraminidase antibodies. Influenza A(H5) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have spread widely among wild birds and poultry and caused infections in mammals, including humans, raising public health concerns (1). A case of human infection with H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus was reported in Washington, USA during 2025; the patient subsequently died, representing the second fatal A(H5) case in the United States (1,2). A(H1) and A(H5) hemagglutinins (HAs) belong to influenza A virus phylogenetic group 1. Most antibodies targeting the HA stalk, a conserved, membrane-proximal region of HA, are cross-reactive with HAs within the same phylogenetic group (3). Studies have demonstrated that previous influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus infection can provide some protection against H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses (4,5). The emergence of H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus raises questions about whether previous A(H1N1)pdm09 immunity confers similar protection against A(H5) viruses bearing antigenically distinct neuraminidases (NAs). We used a preimmune ferret model to compare cross-protection conferred by previous A(H1N1)pdm09 infection against A(H5) viruses with homologous or heterologous NA subtypes. We conducted all experiments with H5N5 and H5N1 viruses in a Biosafety Level 3 enhanced facility with approval from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee. We intranasally inoculated 12 ferrets serologically naive to seasonal influenza viruses with 103 PFUs of A(H1N1)pdm09 A/Nebraska/14/2019 virus. We confirmed seroconversion 3 months postinfection by using a hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) assay, which detects antibodies that inhibit HA-mediated hemagglutination, with a geometric mean titer of 320 (95% CI 245.3–417.3) (Appendix Figure, panel A). Using previously described multiplex binding assays (6), we detected high levels of antibodies binding to the head of A(H1N1)pdm09, but not HA head or ectodomain from H5N1 or H5N5 viruses, and antibodies binding to N1 NAs from A(H1N1)pdm09 and H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, but not N5 NA from H5N5 virus. In addition, we detected antibodies binding to the group 1 HA stalk derived from A(H1N1)pdm09 virus (Appendix Figure, panels B, C). We then intranasally challenged those animals, referred to as preimmune ferrets, with 104 PFU of H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b A/Washington/239/2024 or H5N5 A/Washington/2148/2025 virus (6 ferrets per virus), alongside naive control groups without previous influenza immunity. We euthanized 3 ferrets per group on day 4 postinfection to assess viral dissemination; we monitored the remaining animals for clinical signs, weight loss, viral shedding in nasal washes, and virus presence in throat and rectal swabs. Severe disease, characterized by lethargy, fever, and substantial weight loss (maximum 13.8% in H5N1 virus inoculated ferrets and 18.4% in H5N5 virus inoculated ferrets), developed in naive ferrets inoculated with H5N1 or H5N5 viruses. We euthanized all animals on postinfection days 5–6 for H5N1 virus–inoculated ferrets and days 6–10 for H5N5 virus–inoculated ferrets after they reached predefined humane endpoints, consistent with previous reports (7,8). In contrast, preimmune ferrets challenged with H5N1 virus exhibited minimal disease, a mean maximum weight loss of 2.4%, and 100% survival (Figure 1, panels A–C). Preimmune ferrets challenged with H5N5 also showed reduced disease severity (mean maximum weight loss 7.6%); however, 1 animal reached a humane endpoint on day 7 postinfection (Figure 1, panels B, C). Preimmune ferrets challenged with either H5N1 or H5N5 virus shed similar levels of virus in nasal wash samples during days 1–4 postinfection (range of mean peak titers 103.8–105.2 PFU/mL) as naive controls but exhibited reduced titers in throat swab samples on day 4 for H5N5 virus and days 2 and 3 for H5N1 virus (Figure 2, panels A, B). Viral clearance from nasal washes occurred 2–4 days earlier in preimmune ferrets. We detected H5N1 virus less frequently in rectal swab samples from preimmune animals than from naive controls, whereas we did not observe that reduction for ferrets infected with H5N5 virus (Figure 2, panels A, B). Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus preimmunity did not substantially reduce viral titers in the upper respiratory tract (nasal turbinates) or soft palate after H5N1 or H5N5 virus challenge (Figure 2, panels C, D). However, A(H1N1)pdm09 preimmunity largely prevented viral dissemination to the lower respiratory tract (trachea and lungs) and extrapulmonary tissues for both viruses, with only sporadic low-level viral detection. However, intestinal viral titers were comparable between preimmune and naive ferrets challenged with H5N5 virus (Figure 2, panels C, D). Detection of group 1 HA stalk antibodies after A(H1N1)pdm09 infection (Appendix Figure), together with previous evidence of HA stalk-mediated cross-protection against disease caused by the influenza A viruses within the same phylogenetic group (3,9), suggests that cross-reactive HA stalk antibodies might contribute to protection against A(H5) viruses. In addition, N1 cross-reactivity might further enhance protection against H5N1 virus. Volume 32, Number 12—December 2026 Research Letter Cross-Protection against Influenza A(H5) Clade 2.3.4.4b Viruses after A(H1N1)pdm09 Infection Suggested citation for this article Abstract We challenged ferrets previously infected with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus with H5N1 or H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses to assess cross-protection. Results show that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 virus immunity conferred partial protection against both viruses, with slightly reduced protection against H5N5 compared with H5N1, potentially reflecting the absence of cross-reactive N5 neuraminidase antibodies. Influenza A(H5) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have spread widely among wild birds and poultry and caused infections in mammals, including humans, raising public health concerns (1). A case of human infection with H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus was reported in Washington, USA during 2025; the patient subsequently died, representing the second fatal A(H5) case in the United States (1,2). A(H1) and A(H5) hemagglutinins (HAs) belong to influenza A virus phylogenetic group 1. Most antibodies targeting the HA stalk, a conserved, membrane-proximal region of HA, are cross-reactive with HAs within the same phylogenetic group (3). Studies have demonstrated that previous influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus infection can provide some protection against H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses (4,5). The emergence of H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b virus raises questions about whether previous A(H1N1)pdm09 immunity confers similar protection against A(H5) viruses bearing antigenically distinct neuraminidases (NAs). We used a preimmune ferret model to compare cross-protection conferred by previous A(H1N1)pdm09 infection against A(H5) viruses with homologous or heterologous NA subtypes. We conducted all experiments with H5N5 and H5N1 viruses in a Biosafety Level 3 enhanced facility with approval from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee. We intranasally inoculated 12 ferrets serologically naive to seasonal influenza viruses with 103 PFUs of A(H1N1)pdm09 A/Nebraska/14/2019 virus. We confirmed seroconversion 3 months postinfection by using a hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) assay, which detects antibodies that inhibit HA-mediated hemagglutination, with a geometric mean titer of 320 (95% CI 245.3–417.3) (Appendix Figure, panel A). Using previously described multiplex binding assays (6), we detected high levels of antibodies binding to the head of A(H1N1)pdm09, but not HA head or ectodomain from H5N1 or H5N5 viruses, and antibodies binding to N1 NAs from A(H1N1)pdm09 and H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, but not N5 NA from H5N5 virus. In addition, we detected antibodies binding to the group 1 HA stalk derived from A(H1N1)pdm09 virus (Appendix Figure, panels B, C). We then intranasally challenged those animals, referred to as preimmune ferrets, with 104 PFU of H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b A/Washington/239/2024 or H5N5 A/Washington/2148/2025 virus (6 ferrets per virus), alongside naive control groups without previous influenza immunity. We euthanized 3 ferrets per group on day 4 postinfection to assess viral dissemination; we monitored the remaining animals for clinical signs, weight loss, viral shedding in nasal washes, and virus presence in throat and rectal swabs. Severe disease, characterized by lethargy, fever, and substantial weight loss (maximum 13.8% in H5N1 virus inoculated ferrets and 18.4% in H5N5 virus inoculated ferrets), developed in naive ferrets inoculated with H5N1 or H5N5 viruses. We euthanized all animals on postinfection days 5–6 for H5N1 virus–inoculated ferrets and days 6–10 for H5N5 virus–inoculated ferrets after they reached predefined humane endpoints, consistent with previous reports (7,8). In contrast, preimmune ferrets challenged with H5N1 virus exhibited minimal disease, a mean maximum weight loss of 2.4%, and 100% survival (Figure 1, panels A–C). Preimmune ferrets challenged with H5N5 also showed reduced disease severity (mean maximum weight loss 7.6%); however, 1 animal reached a humane endpoint on day 7 postinfection (Figure 1, panels B, C). Preimmune ferrets challenged with either H5N1 or H5N5 virus shed similar levels of virus in nasal wash samples during days 1–4 postinfection (range of mean peak titers 103.8–105.2 PFU/mL) as naive controls but exhibited reduced titers in throat swab samples on day 4 for H5N5 virus and days 2 and 3 for H5N1 virus (Figure 2, panels A, B). Viral clearance from nasal washes occurred 2–4 days earlier in preimmune ferrets. We detected H5N1 virus less frequently in rectal swab samples from preimmune animals than from naive controls, whereas we did not observe that reduction for ferrets infected with H5N5 virus (Figure 2, panels A, B). Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus preimmunity did not substantially reduce viral titers in the upper respiratory tract (nasal turbinates) or soft palate after H5N1 or H5N5 virus challenge (Figure 2, panels C, D). However, A(H1N1)pdm09 preimmunity largely prevented viral dissemination to the lower respiratory tract (trachea and lungs) and extrapulmonary tissues for both viruses, with only sporadic low-level viral detection. However, intestinal viral titers were comparable between preimmune and naive ferrets challenged with H5N5 virus (Figure 2, panels C, D). Detection of group 1 HA stalk antibodies after A(H1N1)pdm09 infection (Appendix Figure), together with previous evidence of HA stalk-mediated cross-protection against disease caused by the influenza A viruses within the same phylogenetic group (3,9), suggests that cross-reactive HA stalk antibodies might contribute to protection against A(H5) viruses. In addition, N1 cross-reactivity might further enhance protection against H5N1 virus. Consistent with our findings, limited N5 cross-reactivity has been reported in humans despite detectable N1 responses (10). Further studies using H5-specific HA stalk antigens and functional assays are needed to determine the contribution of cross-reactive antibodies and cellular immunity to protection against zoonotic influenza A viruses. Our findings showed that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 viral infection conferred partial cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 viruses in ferrets, reducing disease severity, lethality, and viral dissemination. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether prior infection with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus provides cross-protection against H5N1 and H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses. Using a ferret model, researchers found that previous A(H1N1)pdm09 immunity conferred partial protection, reducing disease severity and viral dissemination.
