elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估既往感染甲型(H1N1)pdm09 流感病毒是否能提供针对 H5N1 和 H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒的交叉保护,这些病毒由于在 野生鸟类 和家禽中传播以及感染包括人类在内的哺乳动物的能力而引起了公共卫生担忧。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用免疫前雪貂模型来比较先前 A(H1N1)pdm09 感染对具有同源或异源 NA 亚型的 A(H5) 病毒的交叉保护。将 12 只对季节性流感病毒进行血清学检测的雪貂接种 A(H1N1)pdm09 病毒,然后用 H5N1 或 H5N5 病毒进行攻击。还包括先前没有流感免疫力的初始对照组。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员在生物安全 3 级增强设施中使用血凝抑制 (HAI) 测定进行了实验,以确认感染后 3 个月的血清转化。他们还使用多重结合测定来检测与 HA 头部和茎部区域以及 N1/N5 神经氨酸酶结合的抗体。雪貂接受 H5N1 或 H5N5 病毒攻击,并监测临床症状、体重减轻、病毒脱落以及喉咙和直肠拭子中病毒的存在情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示,先前的 A(H1N1)pdm09 感染可对 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒提供部分保护,从而降低疾病的严重程度、致死率和病毒传播。接受 H5N1 攻击的免疫前雪貂表现出最小的疾病,平均最大体重减轻 2.4%,存活率为 100%,而接受 H5N5 攻击的免疫前雪貂的平均最大体重减轻为 7.6%,一只动物在感染后第 7 天达到人道终点。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,先前的 A(H1N1)pdm09 免疫力可能会针对 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒提供一些交叉保护,这可能是由于交叉反应性 N1 神经氨酸酶抗体所致,这与在人类中观察到的交叉反应性 N5 神经氨酸酶抗体的缺失形成鲜明对比。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,A(H1N1)pdm09 感染的免疫力可能对雪貂中的 H5N1 和 H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒提供部分保护,这可以为包括人类在内的哺乳动物中的 监测 病毒和 禽流感 病毒的风险评估策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到雪貂模型使用的限制,该模型可能无法完全代表人类 免疫应答,而且样本量较小,每个病毒组有 6 只雪貂。证据是中等的,因为结果是基于动物模型而不是直接基于人类临床数据。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估既往感染甲型(H1N1)pdm09 流感病毒是否能提供针对 H5N1 和 H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒的交叉保护,这些病毒由于在 野生鸟类 和家禽中传播以及感染包括人类在内的哺乳动物的能力而引起了公共卫生担忧。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用免疫前雪貂模型来比较先前 A(H1N1)pdm09 感染对具有同源或异源 NA 亚型的 A(H5) 病毒的交叉保护。将 12 只对季节性流感病毒进行血清学检测的雪貂接种 A(H1N1)pdm09 病毒,然后用 H5N1 或 H5N5 病毒进行攻击。还包括先前没有流感免疫力的初始对照组。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员在生物安全 3 级增强设施中使用血凝抑制 (HAI) 测定进行了实验,以确认感染后 3 个月的血清转化。他们还使用多重结合测定来检测与 HA 头部和茎部区域以及 N1/N5 神经氨酸酶结合的抗体。雪貂接受 H5N1 或 H5N5 病毒攻击,并监测临床症状、体重减轻、病毒脱落以及喉咙和直肠拭子中病毒的存在情况。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果显示,先前的 A(H1N1)pdm09 感染可对 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒提供部分保护,从而降低疾病的严重程度、致死率和病毒传播。接受 H5N1 攻击的免疫前雪貂表现出最小的疾病,平均最大体重减轻 2.4%,存活率为 100%,而接受 H5N5 攻击的免疫前雪貂的平均最大体重减轻为 7.6%,一只动物在感染后第 7 天达到人道终点。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,先前的 A(H1N1)pdm09 免疫力可能会针对 H5N1 和 H5N5 病毒提供一些交叉保护,这可能是由于交叉反应性 N1 神经氨酸酶抗体所致,这与在人类中观察到的交叉反应性 N5 神经氨酸酶抗体的缺失形成鲜明对比。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,A(H1N1)pdm09 感染的免疫力可能对雪貂中的 H5N1 和 H5N5 clade 2.3.4.4b 病毒提供部分保护,这可以为包括人类在内的哺乳动物中的 监测 病毒和 禽流感 病毒的风险评估策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到雪貂模型使用的限制,该模型可能无法完全代表人类 免疫应答,而且样本量较小,每个病毒组有 6 只雪貂。证据是中等的,因为结果是基于动物模型而不是直接基于人类临床数据。

papers.title: Short-term associations between wild-bird and mammalian high pathogenic avian influenza detection in the United States
papers.abstract: High pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) detections in mammals have raised concern about repeated wildlife spillover and the targeting of mammalian surveillance. We evaluated whether wild-bird detection records contained short-term explanatory and predictive information about mammalian detections in the United States. Public surveillance records from April 2022 to July 2026 comprised 18,523 wild-bird and 815 mammalian detections. Monthly state-level mammalian counts were analysed using negative-binomial mixed models adjusted for seasonality, preceding mammalian detections and state-level heterogeneity. The selected model contained contemporaneous and one-month-lagged same-state wild-bird counts. A doubling of one plus the contemporaneous wild-bird count was associated with a 57.9% increase in the expected mammalian count (95% CI 43.5-73.8%), and a doubling of the preceding-month count with a 15.9% increase (5.2-27.8%). Bordering-state exposure did not improve fit. In a six-month temporal holdout, adding same-state wild-bird exposure reduced mean absolute error by 23.8% and root mean squared error by 27.9%, although total detections remained overpredicted. After exact-row deduplication, the corresponding effects were 59.7% and 13.3%. Wild-bird surveillance records contained short-term, geographically local information about mammalian HPAI detection activity, but the associations do not establish direct transmission and require further calibration before operational forecasting.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决对野生动物 跨物种溢出 高致病性 禽流感 (HPAI) 重复出现的担忧以及对哺乳动物 监测 的需求。该研究旨在评估野鸟检测记录是否可以提供有关美国哺乳动物高致病性禽流感检测的短期解释和预测信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 2022 年 4 月至 2026 年 7 月的公开 监测 记录,其中包括 18,523 种野生鸟类和 815 种哺乳动物的检测。重点是州级哺乳动物计数及其与野鸟检测数据的关联。
elements_zh.methods: 使用负二项式混合模型对每月州级哺乳动物计数进行分析,该模型考虑了季节性、先前的哺乳动物检测和州级异质性。该模型纳入了同期和滞后一个月的同州野生鸟类数量。
elements_zh.main_results: 当期野鸟数量加倍与预期哺乳动物数量增加 57.9% 相关(95% CI 43.5-73.8%),上个月野鸟数量加倍与预期哺乳动物数量增加 15.9% 相关(95% CI 5.2-27.8%)。在为期 6 个月的时间坚持中,尽管总检测量仍然被高估,但增加相同州野生鸟类的暴露使平均绝对误差降低了 23.8%,均方根误差降低了 27.9%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,野鸟 监测 记录包含有关哺乳动物 HPAI 检测活动的短期、地理本地信息。然而,协会并没有建立直接的传播,并且需要在业务预测之前进行进一步校准。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过强调野生鸟类检测数据对哺乳动物 HPAI 活动的潜在预测价值,为 监测 策略提供信息。这可能有助于风险评估和有针对性的监测工作。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据受到 监测 记录的使用以及总检测结果可能过度预测的限制。由于这些限制和进一步校准的需要,研究结果的可信度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决对野生动物 跨物种溢出 高致病性 禽流感 (HPAI) 重复出现的担忧以及对哺乳动物 监测 的需求。该研究旨在评估野鸟检测记录是否可以提供有关美国哺乳动物高致病性禽流感检测的短期解释和预测信息。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 2022 年 4 月至 2026 年 7 月的公开 监测 记录,其中包括 18,523 种野生鸟类和 815 种哺乳动物的检测。重点是州级哺乳动物计数及其与野鸟检测数据的关联。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用负二项式混合模型对每月州级哺乳动物计数进行分析,该模型考虑了季节性、先前的哺乳动物检测和州级异质性。该模型纳入了同期和滞后一个月的同州野生鸟类数量。
analysis_zh.main_results: 当期野鸟数量加倍与预期哺乳动物数量增加 57.9% 相关(95% CI 43.5-73.8%),上个月野鸟数量加倍与预期哺乳动物数量增加 15.9% 相关(95% CI 5.2-27.8%)。在为期 6 个月的时间坚持中,尽管总检测量仍然被高估,但增加相同州野生鸟类的暴露使平均绝对误差降低了 23.8%,均方根误差降低了 27.9%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,野鸟 监测 记录包含有关哺乳动物 HPAI 检测活动的短期、地理本地信息。然而,协会并没有建立直接的传播,并且需要在业务预测之前进行进一步校准。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过强调野生鸟类检测数据对哺乳动物 HPAI 活动的潜在预测价值,为 监测 策略提供信息。这可能有助于风险评估和有针对性的监测工作。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据受到 监测 记录的使用以及总检测结果可能过度预测的限制。由于这些限制和进一步校准的需要,研究结果的可信度中等。

papers.title: Penetration of avian and human influenza A viruses through mucus gel networks in vitro
papers.abstract: Abstract Influenza A viruses (IAVs) remain a public-health concern because of their continuous evolution and zoonotic transmission. Respiratory mucus is the first extracellular barrier encountered by inhaled viruses, yet standardized approaches for studying influenza virus passage through mucus and the infectivity of transferred virus populations remain limited. Here, we established an in vitro virus–mucus penetration assay to analyze IAV interactions with standardized mucin-containing matrices. We used mucus from human Calu-3 airway epithelial cells cultured under air–liquid interface conditions and bovine submaxillary mucin as surrogate matrices. Preparations were normalized by total protein and characterized using biochemical and biophysical methods. We compared a human seasonal H1N1pdm virus with a highly-pathogenic avian H5N1 virus. Viral genome transfer was quantified by RT-qPCR, while retained infectivity was assessed in susceptible cells. Both mucin-containing matrices restricted viral passage compared with control solutions. Viral RNA transfer and retained infectivity varied by matrix and virus, although no statistically significant difference between H1N1pdm and H5N1 was detected within either matrix. Together, these results establish a framework integrating mucus characterization with complementary measurements of viral transfer and infectivity. This approach provides a basis for investigating influenza virus–mucus interactions under controlled conditions and can be extended to other IAV strains and physiologically relevant mucus sources.

The evidence is moderate, as it provides a methodological basis for future research but does not offer definitive conclusions on viral behavior in real-world settings.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Influenza A viruses (IAVs) remain a public-health concern because of their continuous evolution and zoonotic transmission. Respiratory mucus is the first extracellular barrier encountered by inhaled viruses, yet standardized approaches for studying influenza virus passage through mucus and the infectivity of transferred virus populations remain limited. Here, we established an in vitro virus–mucus penetration assay to analyze IAV interactions with standardized mucin-containing matrices. We used mucus from human Calu-3 airway epithelial cells cultured under air–liquid interface conditions and bovine submaxillary mucin as surrogate matrices. Preparations were normalized by total protein and characterized using biochemical and biophysical methods. We compared a human seasonal H1N1pdm virus with a highly-pathogenic avian H5N1 virus. Viral genome transfer was quantified by RT-qPCR, while retained infectivity was assessed in susceptible cells. Both mucin-containing matrices restricted viral passage compared with control solutions. Viral RNA transfer and retained infectivity varied by matrix and virus, although no statistically significant difference between H1N1pdm and H5N1 was detected within either matrix. Together, these results establish a framework integrating mucus characterization with complementary measurements of viral transfer and infectivity. This approach provides a basis for investigating influenza virus–mucus interactions under controlled conditions and can be extended to other IAV strains and physiologically relevant mucus sources.

papers.title: Metagenomic assessment of airborne and surface viral signals and worker acceptability during a partial-lid intervention in a Cambodian live bird market
papers.abstract: Abstract Mechanical defeathering can disperse viral material in live poultry markets, but interventional machine modifications must fit routine work. This nonrandomized field study evaluated partial lids on defeathering machines at Orussey Market, Cambodia, across six sampling days, three with lids and three without. Targeted RT-qPCR and target-enriched metagenomics characterised viral RNA in air samples collected during a three-hour air-sampling period and in nearby surface samples collected before and after that period, while work questionnaires assessed usability. Sequencing detected 73 poultry-associated viral taxa. Influenza A virus, avian coronavirus and rotavirus G together accounted for over 80% of relative metagenomic abundance in 14 of 18 air samples. In air samples, RT-qPCR cycle thresholds correlated inversely with metagenomic relative abundance for avian influenza virus and Newcastle disease virus (Spearman’s ρ = −0.645 and − 0.684, respectively). Airborne richness was descriptively lower on days with lids, but targeted viral detections did not change consistently, and composition profiles overlapped. Surface profiles changed from before to after the air-sampling period on days with and without lids; the study did not establish a lid-associated difference in these changes. All five workers reported discomfort and perceived slower work; none wanted to use the lid in its tested form, although three would continue if it were permanently integrated into the machine. With only three sampling days per condition, the study did not establish a consistent reduction in airborne or surface viral contamination associated with lid use. Future studies should evaluate lids redesigned with workers alongside complementary measures addressing ventilation, hygiene, and clean water and waste management to reduce occupational exposure.

papers.title_zh: 在柬埔寨活禽市场进行部分盖子干预期间,对空气和表面病毒信号以及工人可接受性进行宏基因组评估
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Mechanical defeathering can disperse viral material in live poultry markets, but interventional machine modifications must fit routine work. This nonrandomized field study evaluated partial lids on defeathering machines at Orussey Market, Cambodia, across six sampling days, three with lids and three without. Targeted RT-qPCR and target-enriched metagenomics characterised viral RNA in air samples collected during a three-hour air-sampling period and in nearby surface samples collected before and after that period, while work questionnaires assessed usability. Sequencing detected 73 poultry-associated viral taxa. Influenza A virus, avian coronavirus and rotavirus G together accounted for over 80% of relative metagenomic abundance in 14 of 18 air samples. In air samples, RT-qPCR cycle thresholds correlated inversely with metagenomic relative abundance for avian influenza virus and Newcastle disease virus (Spearman’s ρ = −0.645 and − 0.684, respectively). Airborne richness was descriptively lower on days with lids, but targeted viral detections did not change consistently, and composition profiles overlapped. Surface profiles changed from before to after the air-sampling period on days with and without lids; the study did not establish a lid-associated difference in these changes. All five workers reported discomfort and perceived slower work; none wanted to use the lid in its tested form, although three would continue if it were permanently integrated into the machine. With only three sampling days per condition, the study did not establish a consistent reduction in airborne or surface viral contamination associated with lid use. Future studies should evaluate lids redesigned with workers alongside complementary measures addressing ventilation, hygiene, and clean water and waste management to reduce occupational exposure.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 机械脱毛可以分散活禽市场中的病毒物质,但介入性机器改造必须适合日常工作。这项非随机实地研究评估了柬埔寨奥鲁西市场脱毛机的部分盖子,为期六个采样日,其中三个有盖子,三个没有盖子。靶向 RT-qPCR 和目标富集宏基因组学对三小时空气采样期间收集的空气样本以及该时间之前和之后收集的附近表面样本中的病毒 RNA 进行了表征,同时工作问卷评估了可用性。测序检测到 73 个家禽相关病毒类群。在 18 个空气样本中的 14 个中,甲型流感病毒、禽冠状病毒和轮状病毒 G 合计占相对宏基因组丰度的 80% 以上。在空气样本中,RT-qPCR 循环阈值与 禽流感 病毒和新城疫病毒的宏基因组相对丰度呈负相关(Spearman ρ 分别 = -0.645 和 -0.684)。在戴盖子的日子里,空气中的丰富度明显较低,但目标病毒检测并没有一致变化,而且成分分布重叠。在有盖和无盖的日子里,空气采样期之前和之后的表面轮廓发生了变化;该研究并未确定这些变化与眼睑相关的差异。所有五名工人均表示感到不适并认为工作速度较慢;没有人愿意使用经过测试的盖子,但如果将其永久集成到机器中,则有三个人会继续使用。由于每种情况仅采样三天,该研究并未确定与盖子使用相关的空气传播或表面病毒污染的持续减少。未来的研究应该评估与工人一起重新设计的盖子,以及解决通风、卫生、清洁水和废物管理的补充措施,以减少职业接触。

papers.title: Limited Detection of Influenza A Antibodies in Sandhill Cranes (Antigone canadensis) Wintering in the California Central Valley, USA
papers.abstract: The emergence of clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic H5N1 has led to unprecedented mortality events in crane populations globally. Despite increasing concern, little is known about the prevalence of influenza A virus (IAV) and resulting antibodies in Sandhill Cranes (Antigone canadensis). To address this knowledge gap, we sampled 31 Greater and two Lesser Sandhill Cranes (Antigone canadensis tabida and Antigone canadensis canadensis, respectively) wintering in California’s Central Valley during the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 seasons to assess active infection with IAV. None of the sampled individuals tested positive for infection with IAV via rRT-qPCR. We also sampled 29 Greater and two Lesser Sandhill Cranes for serological evidence of prior exposure to IAV; four Greater Sandhill Cranes tested positive for IAV antibodies via bELISA and antibodies specific to H5 were detected in two individuals. These findings suggest prior exposure, potentially on breeding grounds where crane mortalities related to highly pathogenic H5 have been documented. However, the low seroprevalence observed in this study suggests that the Staten Island, California, wintering population may remain largely vulnerable to future outbreaks, though small sample size does limit the broader applicability of these findings.

papers.source_body_en: The emergence of clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic H5N1 has led to unprecedented mortality events in crane populations globally. Despite increasing concern, little is known about the prevalence of influenza A virus (IAV) and resulting antibodies in Sandhill Cranes (Antigone canadensis). To address this knowledge gap, we sampled 31 Greater and two Lesser Sandhill Cranes (Antigone canadensis tabida and Antigone canadensis canadensis, respectively) wintering in California’s Central Valley during the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 seasons to assess active infection with IAV. These findings suggest prior exposure, potentially on breeding grounds where crane mortalities related to highly pathogenic H5 have been documented. However, the low seroprevalence observed in this study suggests that the Staten Island, California, wintering population may remain largely vulnerable to future outbreaks, though small sample size does limit the broader applicability of these findings.

papers.title: BSP3, a bursal-derived tetrapeptide, promotes avian B lymphocyte proliferation in vitro and enhances antigen-specific antibody responses in mice
papers.abstract: The bursa of Fabricius is a unique central immune organ in avian species, and bioactive peptides derived from this organ play important roles in immunomodulation. However, the identification of novel, structurally simple peptides and their underlying molecular mechanisms remains to be fully elucidated. In this study, a novel tetrapeptide, designated BSP3 (bursal-derived small peptide 3; Leu-Leu-Pro-Gly, LLPG), with a molecular weight of 398.50 (m/z), was isolated from the bursa of Fabricius of White-feathered broiler chickens and identified by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF-MS/MS); its sequence uniqueness was confirmed by BLASTP analysis. In vivo experiments in mice showed that co-immunization with BSP3 and an inactivated H9 subtype avian influenza virus vaccine significantly enhanced serum antigen-specific IgG responses, promoted IFN-γ and IL-4 secretion, and increased antigen-stimulated splenic lymphocyte proliferation. In vitro , BSP3 promoted the proliferation of the chicken B lymphocyte line DT40 at an optimal concentration of 5 μg/mL. Exploratory transcriptome analysis of BSP3-treated DT40 cells identified 1,100 candidate genes with altered expression, which were annotated to RNA processing, actin crosslink formation, and extracellular matrix organization; MAPK signaling was positioned at the core of the pathway interaction network. RT-qPCR validation was consistent with the transcriptome data. In conclusion, BSP3 is a novel bursa-derived tetrapeptide that shows immunomodulatory activity in mice and in avian B cells. Further validation in avian hosts and functional protection studies are warranted before BSP3 can be considered a candidate vaccine adjuvant.

papers.title_zh: BSP3 是一种法氏囊源性四肽,可在体外促进禽 B 淋巴细胞增殖并增强小鼠的抗原特异性抗体反应
papers.source_body_en: The bursa of Fabricius is a unique central immune organ in avian species, and bioactive peptides derived from this organ play important roles in immunomodulation. However, the identification of novel, structurally simple peptides and their underlying molecular mechanisms remains to be fully elucidated. In this study, a novel tetrapeptide, designated BSP3 (bursal-derived small peptide 3; Leu-Leu-Pro-Gly, LLPG), with a molecular weight of 398.50 (m/z), was isolated from the bursa of Fabricius of White-feathered broiler chickens and identified by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF-MS/MS); its sequence uniqueness was confirmed by BLASTP analysis. In vivo experiments in mice showed that co-immunization with BSP3 and an inactivated H9 subtype avian influenza virus vaccine significantly enhanced serum antigen-specific IgG responses, promoted IFN-γ and IL-4 secretion, and increased antigen-stimulated splenic lymphocyte proliferation. In vitro , BSP3 promoted the proliferation of the chicken B lymphocyte line DT40 at an optimal concentration of 5 μg/mL. Exploratory transcriptome analysis of BSP3-treated DT40 cells identified 1,100 candidate genes with altered expression, which were annotated to RNA processing, actin crosslink formation, and extracellular matrix organization; MAPK signaling was positioned at the core of the pathway interaction network. RT-qPCR validation was consistent with the transcriptome data. In conclusion, BSP3 is a novel bursa-derived tetrapeptide that shows immunomodulatory activity in mice and in avian B cells. Further validation in avian hosts and functional protection studies are warranted before BSP3 can be considered a candidate vaccine adjuvant.

news.content_title: Can a bird flu vaccine keep up with a virus that keeps changing?
news.content: Subscribe news videos images take action earthpedia earthsnap Subscribe Bird flu’s continued evolution is driving efforts to develop vaccines that protect against a wider range of strains. Credit: Shutterstock November 10, 2026 Can a bird flu vaccine keep up with a virus that keeps changing? A computer-designed bird flu vaccine protected mice against three H5N1 strains, offering early evidence of broader protection before human trials. ByEric Ralls Founder Follow Earth on Google Governments hold doses of bird flu vaccine in storage for the day the virus starts spreading between people. Each of those vaccines was built around a single virus sample. H5 bird flu, meanwhile, keeps splitting into branches that look different to the immune system. A Cambridge team built a rival vaccine, with active ingredients drawn up by computer instead of copied from one virus. Researchers gave it to mice, then exposed separate groups to three H5N1 viruses spanning two decades of evolution. Every one of those mice lived. Half the mice given the stockpile-style vaccine died after exposure to the clade 1 virus. The study was led by Jonathan Heeney, a professor of research in vaccinology in the Department of Veterinary Medicine at the University of Cambridge. The vaccine comes out of the university spin-out DIOSynVax, where he and several co-authors are employees or shareholders. The tests were in mice and ferrets, and no one has given this vaccine to a person. In an interview with Earth.com, Heeney said vaccine design has spent most of a century looking the wrong way. “For more than 70 years, vaccines against rapidly evolving viruses have largely been designed by looking backwards at the pathogen that already exists,” he said. Stockpiles aim at a virus that moved Bird flu now turns up in wild birds, poultry and mammals on nearly every continent. The H5 family has broken into branches that evolve on their own in Asia, Europe, Africa and the Americas. How dangerous those branches are varies sharply. The clade 2.3.4.4b viruses spreading in the Americas have caused 97 known human cases and three deaths, and most of those infections were mild. These viruses have also spread through dairy herds. The 2.3.2.1e viruses circulating in Southeast Asia have killed more than half the people with reported infections over the past two years. The bird flu vaccines in national stockpiles are matched to single virus samples, picked through the World Health Organization’s influenza program. Those vaccines haven’t been widely tested against the other H5 branches now circulating, the authors wrote. “These vaccines are based on single viral isolates, whereas H5Nx viruses have continued to evolve and diversify into multiple lineages around the world,” Heeney told Earth.com. “In many cases, viral evolution has outpaced the strains on which those stockpiled vaccines were originally based.” An antigen drawn up from a database The part of a vaccine that teaches the immune system has a name: the antigen. Rather than lift one from a single virus, the team pooled the genetic sequences of H5 viruses collected worldwide by surveillance programs. Software then drew up antigens carrying the features shared across the whole group. The vaccine carries mRNA instructions for making three designed antigens. One is based on the outer protein the virus uses to get into a cell, and a second on the protein it uses to get back out. The third is a small protein that helps rouse the immune response. The team screened the candidates in cells, then packaged mRNA encoding the selected antigens inside tiny fat particles, using the same delivery approach as mRNA COVID-19 vaccines. Heeney said the design looks ahead instead of back. He noted that his platform uses computational biology to anticipate viral evolution and design broadly protective vaccine antigens before the next outbreak occurs. Mice survived three different H5N1s The team immunized mice, then exposed them to H5N1 viruses from three branches that have all infected people: clade 1, clade 2.3.2.1e and clade 2.3.4.4b. All mice given the designed vaccine survived exposure to their assigned H5N1 virus, with no weight loss or signs of illness. Four days after exposure, no virus could be recovered from their lungs or spleens. The stockpile-style vaccine matched to 2.3.4.4b protected fully against its own matched virus. Against the 2.3.2.1e virus, 67% of those mice survived, and against clade 1, 50% did. Blood tests pointed the same way. Antibodies from the designed vaccine blocked lab-made stand-ins for eleven H5 branches. Each stockpile-style vaccine covered only its own corner of the family. Ferrets lived without the usual antibody score Ferrets catch and spread flu much as people do, making them an important model for testing influenza vaccines. The team exposed them to a 2.3.4.4b H5N1 taken from an Italian chicken. In the entry protein, it differs from the stockpile vaccine’s strain by four amino acids. Every unvaccinated ferret died or reached the humane endpoint by day eight. So did half of those given the stockpile-style vaccine. All ferrets given the lower dose of the designed vaccine survived without weight loss or fever. One ferret given the higher dose reached the humane endpoint. The oddity sits in the bloodwork. On the day of exposure, those ferrets scored below the antibody level flu researchers treat as protective against that virus. Most survived despite those low antibody readings. Something other than that one measure was carrying the protection, the authors wrote, most likely antibodies against the exit protein working alongside antibodies against the entry protein. Questions before human trials The comparison is not clean, and the authors wrote as much. Their vaccine is mRNA, while the benchmark is a killed whole virus, so dose, formulation and delivery all differ along with the antigen design. Comparing both antigen designs using the same mRNA platform would help isolate the effect of antigen design. The mice also got a single dose of the stockpile-style comparator, a benchmark taken from older work. And the designed vaccine’s edge over the stockpile shots can’t yet be pinned on the antigen design alone. Nobody has measured whether any of this holds in people. The next steps are manufacturing the vaccine to meet regulatory standards and a first trial in humans, Heeney said, and DIOSynVax is raising money to pay for them. The designed antigen sequences are patented. What the virus does in the meantime is the part nobody controls. “It’s when bird flu adapts to live in the airways of mammals that we start to get really nervous,” Heeney said. That is the shift researchers watch for in dairy cows and pigs, and the reason a bird flu vaccine that protects against multiple branches could be valuable. The full study was published in the journal Cell Reports Medicine. —– Like what you read? Subscribe to our newsletter for engaging articles, exclusive content, and the latest updates. news.content: Home News Royal Entertainment Trending World Sports Sci-Tech Health H5N1 bird flu crisis: Far more US dairy workers infected than reported, union warns Fear of deportation and lost wages keeps sick workers untested By Najam-ul-Saqib | Published November 12, 2026 Make us preferred on Google H5N1 bird flu crisis: Far more US dairy workers infected than reported, union warns The true number of cattle ranch and dairy workers infected with H5N1 bird flu in the United States is significantly higher than official government figures show, according to a stark new warning from the United Farm Workers (UFW). A hidden outbreak in Washington Speaking out about an active outbreak in Washington State’s Yakima Valley, union representatives revealed that numerous dairy workers are falling ill without ever being tested. Based on direct worker testimonies, the UFW stated that official case counts severely underestimate the spread of the virus, which has recently been linked to at least one fatality in the region. While the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has officially confirmed 74 human cases nationwide since 2024, advocates insist the real toll on farms is much larger. Fear and financial pressure Several barriers are stopping sick workers from seeking medical help or reporting symptoms. The union noted that an ongoing surge in immigration enforcement in the Yakima Valley has left many agricultural laborers terrified of interacting with public health agencies. Additionally, a lack of paid sick leave and fear of employer retaliation force many laborers to keep working while sick, allowing milk production to continue uninterrupted. Severe symptoms and lack of training Workers have reported symptoms ranging from mild respiratory issues and pinkeye to severe flu-like illness involving high fevers, heavy coughs, and intense bone pain. Although most farms provide basic protective gear like goggles, the union warned that workers urgently need proper safety training and stronger protections as the virus continues spreading to new states. news.content_zh: 美国农场工人联合会 (UFW) 对美国奶制品工人 H5N1 禽流感感染漏报表示担忧,警告称实际病例数远高于官方数据。以华盛顿州亚基马谷为中心的 暴发 导致许多工人因担心被驱逐出境、工资损失和雇主报复而在没有接受检测的情况下患病。症状从轻微到严重不等,包括高烧、剧烈咳嗽和剧烈骨痛。尽管美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 自 2024 年以来已确认 74 例人类病例,但 UFW 坚称对农场的实际影响更大。该工会呼吁改进安全培训并加强对工人的保护,强调需要更好的报告和应对机制来应对日益增长的健康风险。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 13, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Study Identifies Twelve Avian Influenza Genotypes Circulating Across Laos by November 12, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Study Identifies Twelve Avian Influenza Genotypes Circulating Across Laos Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Whole-genome sequencing of 37 H5 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses isolated in Laos between 2019 and 2024 has revealed persistent viral circulation, extensive genetic diversity, and ongoing reassortment across multiple clades and genotypes. High pathogenicity avian influenza viruses belonging to several H5 clades have caused outbreaks in Laos since 2004, with clade 2.3.2.1e H5N1 viruses predominating in the country since 2015. Despite these recurring outbreaks, genomic data on the H5 lineages circulating within Laos after 2018 remained limited. To investigate the genetic characteristics of these circulating pathogens, researchers sequenced 37 isolates collected from 2019 to 2024 and evaluated them using phylogenetic analyses alongside publicly available Lao avian influenza sequences gathered between 2015 and 2024. Discover more Engineering job board Research publication platform Scientific instrument sales Laboratory equipment supplier Learn Engineering Based on gene constellations, the investigators identified 12 distinct genotypes spanning three hemagglutinin clades. These comprised seven genotypes within clade 2.3.2.1e designated E1 through E7, three genotypes within clade 2.3.4.4b designated B1 through B3, and two genotypes within clade 2.3.4.4h designated H1 and H2. Clade 2.3.2.1e H5N1 viruses predominated overall during the study window, generating novel genotypes through reassortment events involving clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 and Eurasian low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses. In contrast to this dominant lineage, clade 2.3.4.4b H5Nx and clade 2.3.4.4h H5N6 viruses were identified only sporadically. Phylogenetic comparisons demonstrated that genetically related clade 2.3.2.1e H5N1 genotypes co-circulated across Laos, Cambodia, and Vietnam, while clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 strains identified in Laos in 2023 clustered with viruses documented in East Asia and North America since 2021. The analysis also highlighted zoonotic and cross-species concerns among specific lineages. Genotype H2, representing a clade 2.3.4.4h H5N6 virus, was genetically similar to H5N6 strains epidemiologically linked to a human infection in Laos and detected in both poultry and human patients in China. Discover more Track Biotech Tour Colleges Donate to Research Find Study Aids Bioengineering consulting services Additionally, genotype E7 was detected continuously from 2022 to 2024, exhibiting the identical gene constellation found in viruses associated with human and mammalian infections in Cambodia and Vietnam. The researchers noted that these findings underscore the persistent circulation and reassortment of H5 viruses in Laos, demonstrating the need for sustained genomic surveillance to track transboundary transmission and zoonotic risks across Southeast Asia. analysis.time: The study analyzed H5 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses isolated in Laos between 2019 and 2024. The publication date of the news report is November 12, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The study focused on Laos, with genomic data also compared across Cambodia and Vietnam. The affected population includes poultry and potentially human patients, as some genotypes were linked to human infections.
analysis.event: A study identified twelve distinct genotypes of avian influenza viruses circulating in Laos between 2019 and 2024. The findings were reported by Bioengineer.org on November 12, 2026, and are based on genomic sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study found persistent viral circulation, extensive genetic diversity, and ongoing reassortment across multiple clades and genotypes. Genotype E7 was continuously detected from 2022 to 2024, and some genotypes were associated with zoonotic and cross-species risks.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study highlights the need for sustained genomic surveillance to track transboundary transmission and zoonotic risks. analysis.brief_en: A study published on November 12, 2026, by Bioengineer.org identified twelve distinct genotypes of avian influenza viruses circulating in Laos between 2019 and 2024. The research involved whole-genome sequencing of 37 H5 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses and phylogenetic analysis, revealing persistent viral circulation, extensive genetic diversity, and ongoing reassortment across multiple clades. Clade 2.3.2.1e H5N1 viruses predominated, generating novel genotypes through reassortment with clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 and Eurasian low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses. Genotype E7 was continuously detected from 2022 to 2024 and was associated with human and mammalian infections in Cambodia and Vietnam. The study also noted that clade 2.3.4.4b and 2.3.4.4h viruses were identified sporadically. The researchers emphasized the importance of genomic surveillance to monitor transboundary transmission and zoonotic risks in Southeast Asia. The findings do not include specific public health responses or interventions but highlight the need for ongoing monitoring.

news.content_zh: Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 11 月 12 日发表的一项研究确定了 2019 年至 2024 年间在老挝传播的 基因组 病毒的 12 种不同基因型。该研究涉及对 37 种 H5 高致病性 基因组 病毒进行全 基因组 测序和系统发育分析,揭示了持续的病毒循环、广泛的遗传多样性以及跨多个分支的持续重配。进化枝 2.3.2.1e H5N1 病毒占主导地位,通过与进化枝 2.3.4.4b H5N1 和欧亚低致病性 禽流感 病毒重配产生新的基因型。2022 年至 2024 年持续检测到 E7 基因型,与柬埔寨和越南的人类和哺乳动物感染有关。该研究还指出,零星发现了进化枝 2.3.4.4b 和 2.3.4.4h 病毒。研究人员强调了 基因组监测 对监测东南亚跨境 传播 和人畜共患病风险的重要性。研究结果不包括具体的公共卫生应对措施或干预措施,但强调了持续监测的必要性。

analysis_zh.location_and_population: 该研究重点关注老挝,还比较了柬埔寨和越南的基因组数据。受影响的人群包括家禽和潜在的人类患者,因为一些基因型与人类感染有关。
analysis_zh.event: 一项研究确定了 2019 年至 2024 年间在老挝传播的 禽流感 病毒的 12 种不同基因型。Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 11 月 12 日报道了该研究结果,并且基于基因组测序和系统发育分析。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 该研究发现持续的病毒循环、广泛的遗传多样性以及跨多个进化枝和基因型的持续重配。2022年至2024年连续检测到E7基因型,部分基因型与人畜共患和跨物种风险相关。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 该研究强调需要持续的 基因组监测 来跟踪跨境 传播 和人畜共患风险。这些发现基于基因组数据和系统发育分析,没有明确提及当前的公共卫生反应或干预措施。

analysis.location_and_population: Oregon, Washington, Yakima Valley.
analysis.event: Oregon logs its first H5N1 case in cows; farmer’s union says human avian flu cases underreported in Washington.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: One person in Yakima Valley, Washington, has died this year from avian flu. No specific case or death counts for H5N1 in cows are reported.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CIDRAP reports on the event, but no explicit details on investigation, testing, or response measures are provided.

analysis.brief_en: CIDRAP reported on November 12, 2026, that Oregon has recorded its first case of H5N1 avian influenza in cows. Additionally, a farmer’s union raised concerns about underreporting of human avian flu cases in Washington, citing one death from avian flu in Yakima Valley this year. The report does not provide specific case or death counts for the H5N1 in cows, nor does it detail investigation or response measures. The information highlights the potential spread of avian influenza to livestock and the possible underreporting of human infections, but no further details on the scope of the outbreak or risk assessment were included.

news.content_title: Humans Might Have a Serious Bird Flu Problem on Their Hands
news.content: Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us? Earlier this week, a resident in Yakima County in Washington State died from bird flu , a highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus. Known in more scientific circles as the H5N1, the virus isn’t nearly as threatening to humans as the Covid-19 coronavirus (whose first victims were similarly located in Washington State back in February 2020). But some experts are growing increasingly concerned that this influenza, which for decades has decimated avian populations (and in more recent years, severely impacted the dairy industry ), could develop into something more sinister. The first known case of H5N1 first appeared in 1996 in flocks of domestic waterfowl in southern China. By its nature as an HPAI virus, H5N1 is tailored to latch on to avian cells rather than mammalian cells, including a human’s. However, things have slowly been changing over the decades, and H5N1 mutations have made the virus much more adept at attacking mammals . The newest threat originated during the depths of the Covid-19 pandemic as H5N1 wreaked havoc on seabirds in Europe . The virus eventually found its way to the U.S. in 2022, and hundreds of millions of birds , both wild and domestic, died as a result. A 2024 study by UC Davis reported that the virus reached the very tip of South America, infecting and killing thousands of elephant seals and leaving their bodies strewn along Argentinian beaches . Of course, elephant seals are famously not birds, and during that same time, bovine populations in the U.S. started exhibiting signs of H5N1 infections, driven by polymerase mutations that allowed for better replication in bovine cells . Concerningly, a 2024 study demonstrated that just a single mutation to the bovine influenza H5N1, specifically the hemagglutinin (the surface protein that drives attachment), could switch the virus’s specificity to target humans. Intermediate species can help the virus make the jump to humans (one theory suggests that this is how Covid-19 spread from bats to humans), and last month ProPublica reported that a recent outbreak of H5N1 at a mink farm in Utah is particularly distressing. Unlike those of cows or elephant seals, mink lungs and airways closely resemble ours at a cellular level, raising fears that the virus could adapt to infect humans more easily. When H5N1 impacted mink and fox farms in Finland and Spain , officials moved to cull the infected populations, killing tens of thousands of animals in the process. But ProPublica says state and federal officials in the U.S. have instead done little to curtail the spread. “Every other country that I’m aware of that has had H5N1 in fur farms, depopulation has happened pretty quickly,” avian influenza researcher Tom Peacock told ProPublica. “The fact that the first instinct wasn’t just to depopulate and figure stuff out later is very concerning to me.” If the worst comes to pass, the Trump Administration has gone out of its way so that the country—and the rest of the world—will be vulnerable to the virus. In May 2025, Robert F. Kennedy, the U.S. Secretary of Health of Human Service and well-known vaccine skeptic, cancelled a $700 million contract with Moderna to develop an mRNA vaccine for H5N1. The tragic death earlier this month came from the H5N1 B.13 genotype variant seen in cows, and a CDC spokesperson speaking with Associated Press said that the virus contained no changes that would make it more contagious—but the threat very much remains. “A bad scenario would be that someone working with cattle brought the ‘regular’ human flu in, got [H5N1] on top of that, and that develops into a mix that can spread but to which people have less immunity,” public health virologist Marion Koopmans told The Telegraph . “The chances of such an event are very low, but it is a concern shared among virologists.” Darren lives in Portland, has a cat, and writes/edits about sci-fi and how our world works. news.content_title: Bird flu viruses gaining function through natural mixing, warn scientists
news.content: The bird flu virus' resurgence began with an 11-year-old. In February 2023, the schoolgirl was admitted to a hospital in Phnom Penh with severe pneumonia – within a day, she was dead. Tests soon revealed that she had contracted avian influenza: Cambodia hadn't reported a human case of bird flu since 2014, but the hiatus was over . Since then, 39 more people have been infected and 15 have died in the Southeast Asian country – a case fatality rate of roughly 40 per cent. Researchers have been scratching their heads as to why, after nine years, this particular stain of H5N1 suddenly started jumping from birds to people again . The strain or clade called 2.3.2.1 had been circulating for almost a decade without spilling into humans. What changed? Now, a paper in Emerging Infectious Diseases offers clues. Scientists say the apparent rise in human cases has coincided with the virus gaining new genetic material and, potentially, new powers of infection, from a second flu virus via a process known as "reassortment". H5N1 has infected millions of wild and domestic birds in recent years - AFP/OSCAR DEL POZO The process is similar to mutation in its impact but technically different. While a mutation arises randomly within the DNA of a single strain of flu, reassortment occurs when the material from two different strains jumble to create a new strain. analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 柬埔寨已有39人感染,15人死亡,病死率约为40%。该病毒已感染全球数百万只鸟类,包括在美国,病毒已传播到奶牛并导致死亡。科学家警告说,重组可能会导致人畜共患风险发生不可预测的变化,而 H5N1 仍然是新的全球 暴发 的首要关注点。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 研究人员正在密切关注 H5N1 的 进化,《新发传染病》中的论文强调重配是一个关键因素。科学家尚未证明重配本身使病毒对人类更具传染性,但他们敦促更好的 监测 来追踪变化及其影响。英格兰和苏格兰已经实施了生物安全措施,美国正在监测奶制品工人中的传播情况。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 13, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Avian Influenza Hemagglutinin Mutation Hotspots Drive Cross-Species Spread and Thermal Resilience by November 12, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Avian Influenza Hemagglutinin Mutation Hotspots Drive Cross-Species Spread and Thermal Resilience Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive study mapping the adaptive landscape of avian influenza A(H9N2) hemagglutinin has revealed how specific amino acid substitution hotspots govern viral cross-species potential, antibody evasion, and environmental thermostability. Avian influenza A(H9N2) has circulated globally across avian hosts for nearly six decades following its initial detection in Wisconsin in 1966. Over subsequent decades, the virus has established widespread endemicity in poultry populations across multiple geographic regions, creating persistent agricultural burdens and public health concerns. Beyond domestic avian infections, H9N2 serves as an established reservoir capable of infecting diverse animal hosts and donating internal gene segments to emerging zoonotic influenza strains, including H5N1 and H7N9. In many poultry-dense settings, H9N2 has become the predominant subtype, complicating disease control because conventional inactivated vaccines frequently fail to provide durable protection against divergent field strains. To address these evolutionary challenges, investigators systematically mapped the genetic determinants within the viral surface glycoprotein that enable H9N2 to alter antigenicity, adapt to mammalian cells, and endure thermal stress. The viral hemagglutinin surface glycoprotein mediates host cell entry and represents the primary target of neutralizing antibodies, placing it at the center of antigenic drift and vaccine formulation. Over prolonged circulation, H9N2 hemagglutinin has diversified into major phylogenetic lineages, including Y439, G1, and BJ94, with BJ94 further dividing into more than sixteen antigenically distinct subgroups exhibiting limited cross-reactivity. To resolve the specific mutational patterns driving this diversity, investigators examined 13,984 full-length hemagglutinin coding sequences retrieved from public databases through June 2025. This curated sequence repository encompassed isolates from four primary host groups: 13,014 sequences from domestic avians, 837 from wild birds, 110 from human clinical cases, and 23 from swine. By aligning these coding sequences with multiple sequence alignment algorithms and segregating them by host origin, the researchers established an extensive baseline to evaluate how natural selection operates across different species boundaries. To quantify amino acid variation across the surface glycoprotein, researchers calculated site-specific Shannon entropy values across all 13,984 sequences, establishing an entropy threshold of 0.2 or greater to classify 179 positions as highly variable substitution hotspots. Each identified site harbored at least two distinct amino acid variants, with residues HA66, HA145, and HA168 exhibiting the greatest diversity. Site 168 displayed the highest overall entropy score of 2.63 across fourteen distinct substitutions, followed by site 145 with an entropy value of 1.81. Cross-species correlation analyses revealed that hotspot substitution profiles in avian isolates closely mirrored those in human isolates, yielding a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.99. Conversely, wild bird isolates displayed the lowest similarity to human isolates, registering a Pearson coefficient of 0.77. At residue 145, serine predominated in wild birds while aspartic acid dominated in poultry and humans. At residue 168, serine predominated in wild birds, alanine in poultry, and human isolates harbored both alanine and asparagine variants, underscoring domestic poultry as an essential transitional reservoir. Discover more Engineering job board Research publication platform Scientific instrument sales Laboratory equipment supplier Learn Engineering Recognizing that conventional evolutionary surveillance methods suffer from intrinsic constraints, the authors developed a high-resolution experimental strategy to interrogate hotspot variation. Standard phylogenetic monitoring remains strictly retrospective, restricted to mutations already established in circulating isolates, while traditional in vitro selections rely upon spontaneous mutagenesis that samples mutational space unevenly. To overcome these limitations, the research team constructed a focused deep mutational scanning library targeting all 179 entropy-defined hotspot sites. Using quick-change site-directed mutagenesis, investigators introduced degenerate random codons into each hotspot position within the hemagglutinin gene of the reverse-genetics plasmid rgBJ16/13, representing the A/chicken/Beijing/16/2013 strain. Plasmid pools generated from at least five hundred bacterial colonies per site were harvested and pooled. The resulting hemagglutinin plasmid library was cotransfected into HEK-293T cells alongside seven complementary genomic plasmids encoding the internal segments of rgBJ16/13 to rescue viable viral progeny, generating a primary passage-zero stock that was subsequently amplified in Madin-Darby canine kidney cells. The resulting deep mutational scanning virus library was evaluated using barcoded subamplicon sequencing with unique molecular identifiers to accurately quantify substitution frequencies. The reverse genetics procedure successfully rescued viral variants across all 179 targeted hotspot positions. While initial rescue efficiency for 91.6 percent of individual hotspot sites proved lower than that of parental wild-type rgBJ16/13, sites HA150, HA198, and HA264 showed significantly enhanced rescue, with HA198 reaching a 2.7-fold increase over wild type. Following amplification, deep sequencing revealed that 94.4 percent of hotspot positions maintained substitution frequencies below one percent, with site HA181 exhibiting the highest frequency at 5.4 percent, alongside elevated frequencies at HA115 and HA179. Comparing sitewise library frequencies to the Shannon entropy of natural strains revealed no significant correlation (Pearson R = 0.092), confirming that the experimental library captured unexplored mutational space beyond circulating strains. In contrast, initial rescue efficiency positively correlated with final amplified frequency (Pearson R = 0.22), confirming the predictive value of rescue dynamics. To identify which hotspot residues mediate escape from humoral immunity, the investigators subjected the viral library to three consecutive rounds of in vitro selection using chicken vaccine antiserum raised against rgBJ16/13 at an eighty percent neutralizing concentration. Deep sequencing performed after three rounds of immune selection revealed that selective pressure focused almost exclusively on substitutions at amino acid position 164. Parallel selection using wild-type virus carrying arginine at position 164 confirmed this focus, enriching for a glutamine substitution across two out of three independent biological replicates. To validate these findings, the authors engineered individual recombinant viruses carrying specific substitutions at position 164 and conducted plaque reduction neutralization tests. Analysis of area under the curve measurements demonstrated that viruses carrying 164Q, 164H, 164V, or 164L escaped neutralization by 164R antiserum, causing an approximately one- to two-fold reduction in neutralizing efficacy. Lineage comparisons further revealed that position 164 possesses distinctive lineage-specific profiles, with arginine dominating Y439, glutamine dominating G1, and BJ94 maintaining both variants, establishing residue 164 as an essential determinant of antigenic drift. The investigation subsequently examined host-dependent viral replication dynamics by serially passaging the mixed hotspot library through five consecutive rounds in two distinct biological environments: mammalian Madin-Darby canine kidney cells and ten-day-old embryonated chicken eggs. Over the five serial passages, viral titers displayed contrasting trajectories, increasing progressively in canine cell culture while showing a relative decrease during propagation in embryonated eggs. Next-generation sequencing performed on fifth-passage viral populations revealed profound, system-specific alterations in substitution profiles. In mammalian cell culture, an asparagine-to-histidine substitution at residue 115 (N115H) underwent rapid positive selection, expanding from baseline library levels to constitute 54.6 percent of the total viral population by the fifth passage. In marked contrast, passaging within embryonated chicken eggs selected for entirely distinct genetic alterations, leading to the enrichment of an S334G substitution to 73.5 percent abundance alongside an L224R substitution at 19.5 percent frequency, demonstrating that host cellular environments impose divergent selective pressures upon the avian influenza mutational repertoire. Statistical correlation analyses of substitution frequencies further illuminated the structural divergence between the two host-passaged viral populations. The fifth-passage population harvested from mammalian cell culture maintained a strong positive correlation with the original input library, registering a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.84, which indicated that despite the strong enrichment of N115H, broad genetic diversity across other hotspot positions was largely preserved. Conversely, passage through embryonated eggs triggered extensive restructuring of the mutational spectrum, yielding a low Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.14 when compared to the starting library. To confirm whether the dominant mammalian mutation conferred a measurable fitness advantage, researchers assessed multi-cycle replication kinetics in confluent canine kidney cells infected at a multiplicity of infection of 0.005. Growth curve analyses across three independent biological replicates demonstrated that recombinant viruses bearing the N115H substitution attained significantly higher infectious titers than parental wild-type rgBJ16/13 at 12, 24, and 36 hours post-infection, establishing that this hotspot substitution enhances viral replication efficiency in mammalian systems. In addition to host adaptation and immune evasion, the researchers evaluated hemagglutinin environmental stability, an essential physical parameter that influences viral persistence, transmission dynamics, and zoonotic potential. To identify substitutions increasing structural resilience, the 179-pool hotspot library was subjected to thermal selection at 52.5 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes, an exposure that inactivates over 90 percent of wild-type rgBJ16/13. Normalized plaque assays revealed that substitution pools at positions 14, 134, 218, 302, and 436 conferred markedly enhanced heat tolerance. Deep sequencing of eleven heat-selected sites—positions 4, 13, 14, 40, 134, 176, 218, 230, 302, 306, and 436—demonstrated a drastic reduction in sequence entropy, yielding single, heat-resistant amino acids. To validate these thermal phenotypes, authors tested purified viral variants carrying I134L and L230S within the receptor-binding domain and V306L within the stem region. Inactivation assays across a temperature gradient from 50 to 55 degrees Celsius confirmed that all three substitutions consistently increased heat resistance relative to wild-type virus. By linking computational entropy calculations derived from natural sequence databases directly to high-throughput experimental mutagenesis and phenotypic selection, this research establishes an integrated functional map of avian influenza hemagglutinin evolvability. The authors noted that whereas residue 164 exhibits extensive polymorphism among circulating H9N2 viruses, this identical position remains strictly conserved across other avian influenza subtypes such as H5 and H7, illustrating why reliance on passive sequence monitoring alone fails to anticipate emerging evolutionary trajectories. Furthermore, the exclusion of conserved epitopes from the library ensured that experimental screening focused specifically on regions possessing genuine adaptive plasticity rather than structural fragility. These findings demonstrate that H9N2 antigenic diversity, cross-species replication competence, and environmental stability are orchestrated by a discrete set of mutable hotspots that can be systematically identified and functionally characterized prior to their widespread emergence in nature. Consequently, the authors conclude that this high-throughput deep mutational scanning framework provides an essential scientific platform for predictive viral risk assessment, proactive molecular surveillance of field strains, and the rational engineering of stabilized, broadly protective next-generation poultry vaccines. To validate these thermal phenotypes, authors tested purified viral variants carrying I134L and L230S within the receptor-binding domain and V306L within the stem region. Inactivation assays across a temperature gradient from 50 to 55 degrees Celsius confirmed that all three substitutions consistently increased heat resistance relative to wild-type virus. By linking computational entropy calculations derived from natural sequence databases directly to high-throughput experimental mutagenesis and phenotypic selection, this research establishes an integrated functional map of avian influenza hemagglutinin evolvability. The authors noted that whereas residue 164 exhibits extensive polymorphism among circulating H9N2 viruses, this identical position remains strictly conserved across other avian influenza subtypes such as H5 and H7, illustrating why reliance on passive sequence monitoring alone fails to anticipate emerging evolutionary trajectories. Furthermore, the exclusion of conserved epitopes from the library ensured that experimental screening focused specifically on regions possessing genuine adaptive plasticity rather than structural fragility. These findings demonstrate that H9N2 antigenic diversity, cross-species replication competence, and environmental stability are orchestrated by a discrete set of mutable hotspots that can be systematically identified and functionally characterized prior to their widespread emergence in nature. Consequently, the authors conclude that this high-throughput deep mutational scanning framework provides an essential scientific platform for predictive viral risk assessment, proactive molecular surveillance of field strains, and the rational engineering of stabilized, broadly protective next-generation poultry vaccines. news.title: Bird flu has caused catastrophic die-offs – could a wave of extinctions follow? - The Guardian
news.rss_summary_html: Bird flu has caused catastrophic die-offs – could a wave of extinctions follow?  The Guardian
news.excerpt_original: Bird flu has caused catastrophic die-offs – could a wave of extinctions follow? The Guardian

news.content_title: Bird flu has caused catastrophic die-offs – could a wave of extinctions follow?
news.content: The remains of a northern gannet, probably a victim of avian influenza, washed up on a beach – H5N1 is now a conservation threat to at least 40 bird species, according to BirdLife International. Photograph: Matthijs Wetterauw/Alamy The remains of a northern gannet, probably a victim of avian influenza, washed up on a beach – H5N1 is now a conservation threat to at least 40 bird species, according to BirdLife International. Photograph: Matthijs Wetterauw/Alamy Bird flu has caused catastrophic die-offs – could a wave of extinctions follow? As the IUCN global conservation body prepares to update its red list of endangered species, scientists explain why calculating the true toll of a pandemic is so hard I t began with the brown skuas. The migratory seabirds had arrived on the sub-Antarctic island of South Georgia in 2023, harbouring a deadly passenger. Within months, the southern elephant seals that had come ashore to breed became sick. Mothers and newborn pups were weak and trembling, with many struggling to breathe. What followed was a horrific mass casualty event, caused by the highly infectious avian influenza (H5N1). By 2025, more than 53,000 female elephant seals had died on South Georgia. That is especially alarming, scientists say, because the island is home to more than half of the global breeding population . A highly potent strain of the bird flu virus, which first began circulating in the northern hemisphere in 2021, has now spread to four of the five main southern elephant seal populations. In some South Atlantic colonies, more than 90% of newborn pups have died , alongside about half of all adult females. A southern elephant seal with a pup at Gold harbour, South Georgia. By 2025, more than 53,000 female elephant seals had died on the island. Photograph: Ashley Cooper/Alamy “This is a horror show for wildlife,” says Ruth Cromie, coordinator of a UN taskforce on avian influenza and wildlife. “The scale of mortality is absolutely unprecedented.” In April, the mass deaths prompted the IUCN red list, the global authority responsible for assessing the extinction risks of wildlife, to downgrade the southern elephant seal’s conservation status by two categories, from “least concern” to “vulnerable”. It was the first time a species has had its extinction risk raised explicitly because of H5N1. Dead elephant seals on South Georgia in January 2026. Photograph: Jane Younger The IUCN listing notes that scientists suspect the global southern elephant seal population has declined by nearly a third, and models suggest many populations will take decades to recover. So far, scientists have found few antibodies to the disease among surviving animals. The southern elephant seal is just one species that has suffered catastrophic die-offs since H5N1 began burning its way through the world’s wildlife, killing hundreds of thousands of animals , if not millions. Avian influenza is now a threat to at least 40 bird species, according to BirdLife International , a global conservation partnership. And yet, no other animal – seal or bird – has seen its conservation status changed. But scientists warn that does not mean there are not more species being pushed to the brink by this deadly pathogen. A ssessing a species’ conservation threats is a painstaking scientific and bureaucratic process. To date, the red list has analysed nearly 176,000 species’ extinction risks, and aims to reach 260,000 species by 2030, as well as 142,000 reassessments. Most species are only reassessed by a panel of expert scientists once every decade or so – no matter the emerging threats they may face. The red list itself is updated two to three times a year. Birds are the exception. BirdLife International serves as the authority for assessing the world’s 11,000-plus bird species, reviewing hundreds of birds every year. For that reason, our understanding of the extinction risks of birds is better than for any other animal group. In an epidemic where birds are the foremost victim, that is obviously convenient. But there can still be a lag when deaths are coming faster than scientists can convene and publish under peer review. “We still need to get these things out there,” says Rob Martin, senior red list officer at BirdLife International. Northern gannets rest next to dead gannets on Rouzic Island, off the Brittany coast, in 2022. Photograph: F Tanneau/AFP/Getty Species are generally “uplisted” when they have experienced a sustained population decline over three generations, a small population is in decline or living within a restricted range, or calculations show that the species could become extinct in the near future, given existing population dynamics. Scientific uncertainty often underlies such reviews. Assessors need to know the animal’s baseline population before they can determine if it has crossed a threshold towards extinction. For many species, such figures are in short supply. And without knowing a species’ starting point, it is difficult to calculate the true toll of an outbreak. Scientists with BirdLife International say they are now focused on reassessing four species that have suffered H5N1 outbreaks large enough to affect their conservation outlook: the great skua, northern gannet, Peruvian pelican and Humboldt penguin. Great skuas courting on the Shetland Islands, off Scotland. Photograph: BSIP/Universal/Getty In Scotland, home to more than half of the world’s great skuas , the population of monitored colonies fell by 76% between 2021 and 2023. Meanwhile, the northern gannet, the largest seabird native to the North Atlantic, declined dramatically in two breeding populations in the UK as bird flu spread: by 43% at Bass Rock in Scotland between 2021 and 2024 and 47% at Grassholm in Wales between 2015 and 2024. These are two of the largest northern gannet colonies, and extrapolating from such figures would imply a steep population fall, say BirdLife International assessors, potentially qualifying the species for uplisting from “least concern”. But when scientists took a broader look , they found that the entire north-eastern Atlantic population had declined no more than 17% between 2013 and 2024. “Rushing to judgment a few years ago, with only partial data available and no sense of whether the whole population was declining, would have been premature and could have led to a misclassification,” BirdLife International scientists say. Martin cautions that it is important to prevent “kneejerk” uplisting after a mass mortality event, as listings such as “critically endangered” can trigger dozens of conservation funding proposals and divert government spending. “We need it to be a tool that the community can reliably use and say ‘we trust this,’” he says. Municipal workers collect dead pelicans in Lima, Peru, in November 2022 as another struggles to move. At least 13,000 birds had died by then along Peru’s Pacific coast. Photograph: G Pardo/AP About a fifth of the pelican population living in Peru’s marine protected areas are thought to have succumbed to bird flu in 2022 and 2023. But the Peruvian pelican is considered an abundant bird. “It’s difficult to get accurate numbers for the population pre- and post- [the H5N1 outbreak] because they’re in quite isolated areas without sufficient funding for monitoring,” says Martin. Counting the dead often poses an even greater hurdle, especially for migratory species that travel vast distances over oceans. “You usually don’t find most of the dead birds. If they die at sea, they’re lost,” says Wouter Langhout, a policy consultant at BirdLife International. The flightless Humboldt penguin, which spends most of its life on land, has made such tallies easier. In 2023, scientists counted nearly 3,000 dead penguins along Chile’s coasts, prompting another review of the already vulnerable species, which was last assessed in 2020. E ven when population and mortality numbers are easy to come by, spectacular mass die-offs – as gruesome as they may be – do not guarantee a species is inching towards extinction. For long-lived seabirds, large waterbirds and elephant seals that are slow to reproduce and late to sexually mature, a large loss of breeding adults can translate into severe population declines in just three generations – a key red-list criterion for uplisting. But fast-reproducing animals or those with abundant populations may be spared such long-term consequences, especially if more adult males die than fertile females. Antarctic fur seals in heavy snow on South Georgia as king penguins pass by. Photograph: Ben Cranke/naturepl.com In the case of the Antarctic fur seal, for example, far more males have succumbed to the disease than breeding females, says Jaume Forcada, a marine mammal expert and population biologist at the British Antarctic Survey who has studied Antarctic fur seals for 25 years. That is because male and female fur seals behave very differently. Whereas the males come ashore for about two months, often battling with one another on beaches, “when females arrive, they pup, and then they go out very quickly. They’re less exposed to other animals apart from the moment when they are rearing their pup,” Forcada says. In turn, “the males were very severely affected, whereas the females were absolutely fine. It’s like it was a completely different species. It hadn’t affected them.” If scientists uncover a population decline that would warrant uplisting, attributing it to avian influenza may not be cut and dried, Martin cautions. For example, BirdLife recently reassessed the African penguin, which was heavily affected by avian influenza. Although it was uplisted to critically endangered in 2024, assessors determined that food loss linked to commercial fisheries and the climate crisis – not bird flu – ultimately drove its decline. The carcass of an endangered Humboldt penguin on a beach in Vina del Mar, Chile, in 2023. Photograph: R Garrido/Reuters The 3,000 dead Humboldt penguins in Chile have also triggered debate among scientists. Penguins often drown in gill nets and 2023 was also an El Niño year, which may have had a hand in the birds’ deaths. “That year could be described as a ‘perfect storm’, which produced highly unfavourable conditions for Humboldt penguins,” says Alejandro Simeone, a scientist in the IUCN’s penguin specialist group. “While it is quite possible that some Humboldt penguins died from [avian influenza], current evidence makes it difficult to assess the true extent of the virus’s role in this decline,” Simeone says. I n the end, it may not be the most visible victims that are in the greatest peril. Birds with tiny isolated populations – often those inhabiting small islands – can quickly move towards extinction even if only a handful of individuals die. “For species that are already under threat and declining for other reasons, and then you put in something like avian influenza, that might be the thing that then pushes them over the edge ,” Cromie says. To date, scientists say they are not yet aware of any such cases from bird flu, but are anxiously monitoring Australia , where H5N1 was first detected on the mainland in June. The endangered regent honeyeater in an aviary at Sydney’s Taronga zoo this year, where vulnerable species of birds are being vaccinated against bird flu. Photograph: B de Marchi/AAP “A lot of Australian species still do have quite wide ranges, but there’s a very specific habitat that they rely on,” Martin says. The country is also home to a number of critically endangered birds that can be found nowhere else in the world, such as the orange-bellied parrot and the regent honeyeater. Waiting for uplisting, Cromie adds, may miss the bigger picture. “We have to be focusing on taking these other pressures off,” she says. “If we become very fixated on only waiting to do something because of a change of status, there’s such a lag there. We’ve got to be doing other things at the same time.” Already, fur seals and dolphins in Australian waters have begun to die from bird flu. And things are about to get worse for the now-vulnerable southern elephant seal. In August, the government’s Australian Antarctic Division said it would evacuate its research station on Macquarie Island in anticipation of mass seal die-offs if H5N1 reaches its shores. Macquarie is the last stronghold of southern elephant seals that, until recently, had remained untouched by the virus. Though the risk to human health is low, the agency said it hoped to prevent psychological distress for staff who could witness the deaths of thousands of newborn seal pups. About 5,000 of the world’s largest little penguin colony, on Australia’s Phillip Island, were vaccinated against H5N1. Photograph: Getty The next update to the list is due on 26 November, and proposals for new uplistings will next be discussed in January and February 2027. “Our biggest fear is always that we completely miss something that suddenly is critically endangered. That’s what we’re guarding against,” Martin says.
